front/choices/a-folktale/0/text.source: There’s this old tale, about an old herb tender from Marshedge that tricks a fen-troll into eating an enchanted seedpod. She promises to go get the troll more food if he promises to then let her go. Of course, the troll breaks his word and tries to eat her, but the seedpod bursts into a mass of gwir-nettles when he does.

front/choices/a-folktale/1/text.source: You can learn the secret of the enchanted seedpods, but need one of the following:

front/choices/a-folktale/marshedge-herba.source: A Marshedge herbalist, steeped in lore, to teach you the ritual

front/choices/a-folktale/spirit-gwir/tex.source: The spirit of a gwir-nettle, friendly or bound, to reveal the secrets of its birth

back/choices/intro/0/text.source:
When you **_soak a pair of gwir-nettle seedpods in_** **_your own blood, whisper secrets over them, and_** **_say the words of power_**, they become truth seeds (*magical)*.

When you and another **_each eat a truth seed and_** **_make promises to each other_**, the seeds stay in your guts and ensure that the promises are kept.

When you **_break your promise_**, the truth seed in your gut sprouts violently into a full-grown gwir-nettle, dealing 1d10+3 damage with advantage (*messy*, ignores armor) and now you’ve got a gwir-nettle growing out of you.

If the **_other party breaks their promise_**, they suffer the same fate.

front/choices/azure-hand/0/text.source: A thick staff of gray metal, topped with a plate of aetherium in the shape of a stylized hand. The palm is embossed with a cloud and lightning bolt, and the whole thing is more than a little topheavy. It smells of ozone, and your spine never ceases to tingle in its presence.

front/choices/azure-hand/1/text.source: When you **_bear the Azure Hand_**, you sense sources, currents, and reservoirs of energy much like you sense the pull of gravity or the position of your own hand. You can closely study such energy and Seek Insight about it.

front/choices/azure-hand/2/text.source:
When you **_brandish the Azure Hand at a source of elemental energy_**, roll +CON: **on a 10+**, you gather the energy about the Hand in a swirling vortex for as long as you grip the staff or until you choose 1 from the list below; **on a 7-9**, as a 10+, but the vortex is unstable and maintaining it requires all your focus.
- Direct the energy into a vessel able to contain it
- Discharge the energy harmlessly into the earth
- Fling the energy, rolling +INT to Let Fly (*thrown*, *dangerous*), inflicting damage and other effects of the GM’s choosing
- Use the energy to fuel or empower some other magic.

**On a 6-**, instead of marking XP, mark 1:

back/choices/consequences/hand-c1/text.source: You are burned by the power you attempt to wield. Mark a debility and take 2d4 damage (ignores armor).

back/choices/consequences/hand-c2/text.source: You become bound to the staff. You can call it to your hand from up to *far* range, but you fully suffer the effects of any harm or magic visited upon it.

back/choices/consequences/hand-c3/text.source: Your eyes become a solid bluish white, darkening or brightening with your mood. You now see energy patterns, glowing brightly, which can obscure facial expressions and other details unless you focus.

back/choices/consequences/hand-c4/text.source: Your skin takes on a bluish tint; your hair is steaked with white; the air about you thrums with power. Sensitive beings can easily sense your presence, even from afar.

back/choices/consequences/hand-c5/text.source: Henceforth, any storm in your presence is unnaturally strong. If you spend a summer or a winter in a steading or within a day’s march of one, the steading loses 1d4-1 Surplus due to storms.

back/choices/consequences/hand-c6/text.source: Your body pulses with barely controlled energy. Henceforth, when you **_roll +CON and get a 6-_**, you unleash bolts of elemental power all about you (1d10 damage, *near*, *area*, *forceful*, *dangerous*) in addition to whatever else the GM says.

front/choices/beaded-satchel/0/text.source: Made of thick, stiff leather and decorated with impossibly fine beadwork. The pattern shows a fruit-laden tree sheltering various game and produce and grains. The specifics often change when you aren’t looking.

front/choices/beaded-satchel/1/text.source: The satchel is home to a number of spirits of autumn and plenty. To unlock the satchel’s secrets and gain the spirits’ aid, you must…

front/choices/beaded-satchel/imbibe-prod.source: … imbibe a prodigious, dangerous quantity of alcohol.

front/choices/beaded-satchel/thoroughly-.source: … while thoroughly drunk, commune with the tethered spirits (**Instinct** to be genuinely, awkwardly caring and giving) and win their friendship.

front/choices/beaded-satchel/feed-satche.source: … feed the satchel 1 Surplus of freshly harvested foodstuffs (which shouldn’t possibly fit, but does).

front/choices/beautiful-scroll/0/text.source: Inside a case of carved ivory rests a scroll made of fine, almost gauzy wool. It is full of glyphs and diagrams, imprinted with rich dyes of red and black and yellow. The diagrams seem to depict some sort of meditative practice, resulting in some kind of familiar spirit?

front/choices/beautiful-scroll/1/text.source: To unlock the mysteries of this scroll, you must…

front/choices/beautiful-scroll/spend-few.source: … spend a few months practicing the meditative techniques it describes.

front/choices/beautiful-scroll/describe-.source: … describe and name the tiny spiritconstruct that you wish to create:

front/choices/beautiful-scroll/permanent.source: … permanently sacrifice 2 HP to invest the tulpa with "life."

back/choices/intro/0/text.source: You have created a tulpa, which you treat as a follower. Pick 2 additional tags, an instinct, 2 additional moves, and its cost.

front/choices/blackwood-fetishes/0/text.source:
A pair of wooden figurines, carved from blackwood and worn smooth with age and use. A whitish shaft has been driven into the top of each figurine’s head, and the eyes and forehead of each are stained a rusty, reddish color.

The figurines resist all mundane attempts to damage them. Such attempts might mar them slightly, but their forms hold fast.

front/choices/blackwood-fetishes/1/text.source: When you **_mark a figurine’s eyes with blood and likewise mark your own eyelids_**, you see through the eyes of the figurine whenever you close your eyes, for as long as the blood remains.

front/choices/blackwood-fetishes/2/text.source: When you **_anoint a figurine with your own blood and then sleep in its presence_**, roll +CON: **on a 10+**, you dream lucidly of the spirit in the figurine, which speaks an archaic but intelligible dialect—it might be persuaded to reveal its name, or the name of its fellow spirit, or the method of calling them forth; **on a 7-9**, you dream of the spirit, but the dream is fleeting, strange, and disorienting—ask the GM what you learn of the spirit.

front/choices/blackwood-fetishes/3/text.source: When you **_learn the name of one of the bound spirits_**, or the sign that draws them forth and binds them, mark 1:

front/choices/blackwood-fetishes/4/text.source: When you **_make the last mark_**, you unlock the mysteries of the Blackwood Fetishes and can use Call Forth and Command (see reverse).

front/choices/blood-quenched-sword/0/tex.source: An ancient blade of deep red bronze, its pommel etched with symbols like those that the Hillfolk use to decorate their drinking horns. It thrums in its scabbard, wanting nothing more than to be drawn and to burn like a fire, quenching itself in the blood of foes.

front/choices/blood-quenched-sword/1/tex.source: When you **_draw the Blood-quenched Sword_**, it leaps from its sheath before any present have time to even blink, and must spill blood before you can return it to its sheath.

front/choices/blood-quenched-sword/2/tex.source: When you **_spill your own blood in order to return the Sword to its sheath_**, take 1d4 damage (ignoring armor) and the scars from the cut never fade.

front/choices/blood-quenched-sword/3/tex.source: When you **_strike first in a fight with the Blood-quenched Sword_**, gain advantage on your first roll.

front/choices/blood-quenched-sword/4/tex.source: When you **_sheathe the Sword after using it to kill a living, bleeding foe_**, mark 1 unless you have already done so since the last sunset:

back/choices/consequences/sword-c1/text.source:
You lose yourself in a blood-rage, no longer distinguishing between friend, foe, and bystander.

When you **_attack the nearest living creature_**, you have advantage on damage rolls.

When you **_attempt to stay your hand_**, roll +WIS: **on a 10+**, you do so, and can choose to calm yourself and end the rage with a few moments focus; **on a 7-9**, you stay your hand, but must choose a different target for your rage; **on a 6-**, attack without mercy or doubt.

back/choices/consequences/sword-c2/text.source: Pick someone who survives this battle (friend or foe). You are convinced that they covet the Blood-quenched Sword. Until you put them in their place, you are either *dazed* or *miserable* (your choice).

back/choices/consequences/sword-c3/text.source: Your instinct becomes "Paranoia: to accuse someone of plotting against or wanting to steal the Blood-quenched Sword, and do something about it."

back/choices/consequences/sword-c4/text.source: You can no longer sleep or rest without the Blood-quenched Sword at hand.

back/choices/consequences/sword-c5/text.source: You no longer gain sustenance from food. When you **_slay a living, bleeding creature with the_** **_Sword_**, hold 1 Sustenance (max 3). When you would consume a ration, lose 1 Sustenance instead.

back/choices/consequences/sword-c6/text.source: You can always ask the GM "Does this NPC disrespect me or intend to do me harm?" and the GM will answer honestly "Yes" or "No." If they answer "Yes," gain advantage to end their life and take disadvantage to do anything else.

front/choices/bow-with-no-string/0/text.source: A short flatbow made of pale blue metal, rigid and gracefully curved even though it’s unstrung. There aren’t even hooks where you *could* attach a string.

front/choices/bow-with-no-string/1/text.source: It seems to be of little use, but there is more to this bow than meets the eye. To unlock its mysteries, you must…

front/choices/bow-with-no-string/acquire.source: … acquire a glove of aetherium, properly attuned to the bow.

front/choices/bow-with-no-string/learn-s.source: … learn the secret word that activates the bow.

front/choices/bow-with-no-string/charge-.source: … charge the bow with lightning, risking harm to the bow or yourself.

front/choices/bow-with-no-string/spend-f.source: … spend a few weeks practicing, risking all manner of collateral damage in the process.

back/choices/intro/0/text.source:
When you **_speak the secret word_**, the bow activates and hums ominously. When you then **_wear the aetherium glove and grasp where the_** **_string should be_**, a crackling line of lightning appears between the horns.

When you **_draw back the lightning_**, a thunderbolt forms where an arrow should be. It manifests over the course of a deep breath, after which you can Let Fly.

You must charge the bow with lightning to replenish its ammo.

When you **_draw back the lightning for at least_** **_ten deep breathes_**, deplete your ammo. Your next shot deals +1d4 damage (+*area*, +*dangerous*), but if you roll snake eyes to Let Fly, the bow explodes (3d6 damage, *reach*, *area*, *forceful*, *loud*).

front/choices/carvings-in-a-cave/0/text.source: At the bottom of a sinkhole is a limestone cave. A moldering skeleton slumps against one wall, showing signs of having been hanged. Yet carved into the cave walls are runes, caked over with mineral deposits.

front/choices/carvings-in-a-cave/1/text.source: You can study the runes and learn the secrets they contain, but...

front/choices/carvings-in-a-cave/careful.source: … you must carefully restore the runes over a few weeks of work.

front/choices/carvings-in-a-cave/risk-ru.source: … you risk ruining them as you work.

front/choices/carvings-in-a-cave/deciphe.source: … you must decipher the old writings, which are similar to Stone Lord runes.

front/choices/carvings-in-a-cave/then-ta.source: … it will then take a few days of study.

back/choices/intro/0/text.source:
When you **_touch a dying, intelligent being, speak_****_ing their name and words of binding_**, roll +INT: **on a 10+**, you bind their soul to your flesh; **on a** **7-9**, you bind their soul but weaken yours— reduce your max HP by 1d4+1.

Your flesh can bind a number of souls equal to your CON. They manifest in dreams and struggle for control when your mind or body are weak. Write their names here:

When you **_roll a 6- on Death’s Door_**, you can release a bound soul to go through the Last Door in your place. If you do, you survive as if you rolled a 7-9. Your body, though, still bears the marks of that which would have killed you.

front/choices/chain-of-rusty-locks/0/tex.source: A chain, six links long, each link hung with a corroded bronze padlock. 1d4+1 locks bear a stylized face, frozen in a rusty grimace. The keys to these locks are lost to the ages.

front/choices/chain-of-rusty-locks/1/tex.source:
When you **_hold one of the face-adorned locks and_** **_look into its eyes_**, you can hear the voice of the departed soul bound within: hateful, desperate, pleading to be set free.

You can master these locks by…

front/choices/chain-of-rusty-locks/convi.source: … convincing one of the shades to reveal how it was captured.
… convincing a shade to reveal what happens when a lock is opened.

front/choices/chain-of-rusty-locks/findi.source: … finding a way to open the locks.

back/choices/intro/0/text.source:
When you **_smear the blood of the dying onto an_** **_open Lock of Sajua and then close the lock_**, roll +CON: **on a 10+**, their soul is bound in the lock; **on a 7-9**, their soul is bound, but all mundane metal in your presence rusts or tarnishes, corrodes and weakens.

When you **_extract a promise from a bound soul_** **_and then open the lock that binds it_**, the soul is compelled to fulfill the letter of its promise before it goes its own way. Tell the GM to treat it as a ghost (though not necessarily as a follower); the open lock serves as its tether, at least for now.

Each time you release a soul, mark 1 Disturbance and roll 1d6. If you roll less than your Disturbance, you hear the call of the Pale Hunter in the distance. Expect a visit soon.

front/choices/clear-natural-pool/0/text.source: High in the hills, a stream of snowmelt fills a deep pool in the rocks before flowing on. At the bottom of the pool is a large deposit of lodestone. Rusted old blades (many sized for giants) can be seen clinging to the lodestone.

front/choices/clear-natural-pool/1/text.source: There is magic here; to unlock its secrets, either...

front/choices/clear-natural-pool/spend-w.source: … spend a week or so experimenting at the pool, then roll +INT: **on a 10+**, you figure it out; **on a 7-9**, no luck; **on a 6-**, you are interrupted by danger; or...

front/choices/clear-natural-pool/get-fir.source: … get a firsthand account of the pool’s powers in use.

back/choices/intro/0/text.source:
When you **_cut yourself with iron or steel and toss_** **_the blooded metal into the pool_**, you form a bond with the waters. So long as you carry a vial of the pool’s water on your person, you are protected by the ward of still waters.

When you are so protected and **_subject to magic_** **_that attempts to sense or affect your thoughts,_** **_actions, or emotions_**, the magic targets the still waters of the pool instead—possibly befuddling the magic’s source.

Each time the ward of still waters protects you, mark 1 Strain and then roll 1d6. If your roll is less than your current Strain, the water you carry loses its potency. When you **_return to the pool_** **_and renew your bond_**, clear all Strain.

front/choices/cloak-richly-embroidered/0.source: An exquisitely fine wool, dyed a pale blue-gray and embroidered with stylized clouds. The edge boasts blue-white runes stitched with aetherium wire. It feels damp, smells of rain and ozone, and flutters in a breeze that isn’t there.

front/choices/cloak-richly-embroidered/1.source: When you **_don the cloak_**, you become aware of the presence bound within, thrumming and impatient. To unlock the mysteries of the cloak, you must...

front/choices/cloak-richly-embroidered/l.source: … learn the name of the bound spirit.

front/choices/cloak-richly-embroidered/d.source: … decipher the word of command, embroidered in ancient Maker-script.

front/choices/cloak-richly-embroidered/b.source: … bend the spirit to your will, risking its (destructive) escape.

back/choices/intro/0/text.source: When you **_wear the cloak and speak the word of_** **_command_**, the storm-spirit in the cloak springs to life and obeys you as a follower. It never wants to land; you must spend its Loyalty or Persuade it.

front/choices/copper-banded-staff/0/text.source: A short staff, about 4 feet tall, tapering towards the tip and made of blackened oak with a strange metallic sheen. A dozen bands adorn it, made of corroded copper, caked in verdigris and crumbling away in spots. The bands are embossed with runes of power, some of them worn away or obscured.

front/choices/copper-banded-staff/1/text.source: The staff still tingles with power. To unlock its mysteries you must…

front/choices/copper-banded-staff/figure.source: … figure out the shape of the missing and damaged runes.

front/choices/copper-banded-staff/replac.source: … replace the bands with new ones of rune-embossed aetherium.

front/choices/copper-banded-staff/hold-f.source: … hold fast as lightning courses through the staff, attuning to its magic (you risk serious burns or at least flinching and letting go).

front/choices/copper-banded-staff/spend-.source: … spend a few days practicing with the charged-up staff.

back/choices/intro/0/text.source:
When **_lightning courses through the staff,_** it holds 3 Charge (max 3).

When **_the staff holds Charge and you focus your_** **_will and senses through it_**, you can sense iron, steel, cobalt, and nickel within *near* range and move such objects slowly and awkwardly. You can manipulate only items that you could lift with one hand.

When you **_tap into the power stored within the_** **_staff_**, pick 1:

- Extend its effects up to *far* range
- Move items quickly and suddenly, fast enough to attack or defend (*dangerous*)
- Manipulate an object of considerable mass, as much as you can deadlift Each time you tap into the staff’s power, roll 1d6. If you roll higher than the staff’s current Charge, it loses 1 Charge.

front/choices/corroded-spearhead/0/text.source: Hidden away in some vault or cave or Makerruin is a length of copper, heavily corroded and coated with chunks of verdigris. If you squint, you vaguely make out the shape of a spearhead. Oh, and are those the faint traces of runes?

front/choices/corroded-spearhead/1/text.source: To unlock the secrets of this ancient weapon, you must…

front/choices/corroded-spearhead/careful.source: … carefully clean away the corrosion with proper chemics, without destroying the runes as you do so.

front/choices/corroded-spearhead/deciphe.source: … decipher the runes and how they are meant to be charged.

front/choices/corroded-spearhead/infuse-.source: … infuse the restored spearhead with lightning.

front/choices/corroded-spearhead/mount-s.source: … mount the spearhead on a shaft of birchwood.

front/choices/corroded-spearhead/soak-sp.source: … soak the spearhead in your own blood, to claim its power as yours.

back/choices/intro/0/text.source:
When you **_Clash with the aetherium spear and_** **_get a 7+_**, you can mark a debility to blast your foe with lightning, dealing +1d6 damage (*forceful*, *loud*).

When you **point the aetherium spear at your foes** **and bellow a thunderous warcry**, mark a debility and unleash a blast of lightning (*far*, *area*, *force**ful*, *loud*, *dangerous*), rolling +STR to Let Fly instead of +DEX (and you cannot choose to deplete ammo). **On a 6-**, in addition to whatever else the GM says, the spearhead is drained of power and the birchwood shaft is reduced to cinders—clear the last 3 check boxes on the front of this card.

front/choices/cracked-flute/0/text.source: A long, thick flute carved of redwood, with a thin but visible crack along the underside. It easily catches the wind and makes a piping sound. Anyone who plays a few notes on the flute can tell there’s some magic here.

front/choices/cracked-flute/1/text.source: When you **_spend a few days practicing, playing_** **_the flute where the wind can hear you_**, roll +CHA: **on a 10+**, mark 1 circle; **on a 7-9**, mark 1 circle, but you summon an irate zephyr spirit; **on a 6-**, you make no progress but do manage to summon an irate zephyr.

back/choices/intro/0/text.source: When you **_play a tune to make the wind itself_** **_dance_**, the andalau (zephyr spirit) tied to the flute manifests. Treat it as a follower; it holds 1 Loyalty to start. When you **_dismiss the spirit_** **_while it holds no Loyalty_**, the flute splits and falls apart; the andalau is set free.

front/choices/creepy-cave/0/text.source: There’s a cave somewhere—somewhere that the light never shines—where the walls are roiling formations, slick and wet, glinting with veins of red crystal that no longer glows. The stone undulates in the flickering torchlight. Yes, yes, that must be it... a trick of the light, nothing more.

front/choices/creepy-cave/1/text.source: The cave bears the lingering taint of a Thing Below, but has been cut off from its power. To unlock its secrets, you must…

front/choices/creepy-cave/learn-name/tex.source: … learn the name of the Thing Below that once corrupted this place.

front/choices/creepy-cave/stay-here/text.source: … stay here in absolute darkness for at least a full day, despite the nightmares and hallucinations that try your soul.

front/choices/creepy-cave/bring-still/te.source: … bring a still-living, warm-blooded being to the cave and spill its life’s blood on the stones while intoning the name of the Thing Below that once touched this unholy place.

back/choices/intro/0/text.source:
When you **_cruelly kill a warm-blooded being_** **_in the cave,_** one of similar size to yourself, and **_smear both its blood and yours upon the stones,_** mark 1:

- Gain unholy resilience: increase your max HP by 2 and gain +1 armor against anything but bronze.
- Gain one of your victim’s physical traits (their strength, their speed, their looks, their strong heart, etc.).
- Heal yourself of a permanent injury (regrowing a limb, removing a scar, fixing a bad knee, etc.). **_Each time you use this power_**, mark all three debilities. With each use, some of the red crystal vanishes from the cave. After the third use, the crystal and the cave’s power are gone.

front/choices/crumbling-arch/0/text.source: On a rare dry spot in Ferrier’s Fen, besieged by foulness, is an ancient arch that still—improbably—stands. Lichen and moss grow thick and healthy, but the keystone remains clear, engraved with a sigil that makes the eyes water and that drives evil away.

front/choices/crumbling-arch/1/text.source: You can learn the secrets of the sanctifying mark, but to do so you must…

front/choices/crumbling-arch/purify-your.source: … purify yourself in fresh, clean water.

front/choices/crumbling-arch/calm-mind/t.source: … calm your mind, gaze upon the sigil, and roll +WIS: **on a 10+**, the sigil becomes clear; **on a 7-9**, the sigil will become clear after a few more days in contemplation; **on a 6-**, the sigil is beyond your ability to learn.

front/choices/crumbling-arch/spend-few/t.source: … spend a few days memorizing and practicing the sigil.

back/choices/intro/0/text.source:
When you **_mark an object with the sigil of_** **_sanctification_**, it repels beings of darkness, chaos, and death. Each time you place the mark, part of you (eyes, hair, skin, tongue, etc.) becomes paler, eventually turning a shocking white.

When a **_being of darkness, chaos, or death first_** **_tests the power of your mark_**, roll +INT: **on a 10+**, all such creatures are kept at bay so long as your mark remains inviolate; **on a 7-9**, such creatures feel the urge to flee and are held back for now, but powerful entities can force themselves to ignore it.

front/choices/demonhide-cloak/0/text.source:
A tattered cloak, stitched from a motley patchwork of unfamiliar hides and leather. Shifting odors waft from it: damp earth, ozone, musk, sulfur, rust, rot.

It is not a glamorous garment. Anything but.

front/choices/demonhide-cloak/1/text.source: When you **_wear the Cloak_**, its armor applies against demons in all cases, even if their attacks are piercing or ignore armor.

front/choices/demonhide-cloak/2/text.source: When you **_draw up the hood of the Cloak_**, you see clearly in darkness.

front/choices/demonhide-cloak/3/text.source: When you **_wrap the Cloak tightly about your person_**, you pass unnoticed by all so long as you move calmly and carefully and keep out of direct, harsh light. In retrospect, those you pass may recall a strange smell.

front/choices/demonhide-cloak/4/text.source: When you **_flay the hide from a demon, tan it, and sew it onto the cloak_**, mark 1:

front/choices/demonhide-cloak/5/text.source: When you **_make the last mark_**, you unlock the mysteries of the Cloak and can use The Flesh Remembers (see reverse).

back/choices/consequences/cloak-c1/text.source: You experience an overwhelming vision, from the point of view of a demon sewn into the Cloak. Ask the GM what you see and when you come to.

back/choices/consequences/cloak-c2/text.source: A number of seams fray and tear. The Cloak loses its powers until you sew a new piece of

back/choices/consequences/cloak-c4/text.source: The Cloak’s stench grows stronger, noticeable even when you go unseen and unheard. You smell faintly of the Cloak even when you aren’t wearing it.

back/choices/consequences/cloak-c5/text.source: You become incapable of fear while wearing the Cloak. If you **_wear the Cloak during a session_**, your instinct becomes "Recklessness: To act with no regard to danger or consequence."

back/choices/consequences/cloak-c6/text.source: You begin to hear the voices of the dark creatures sewn into the Cloak. The Cloak becomes a follower (see below). When you would mark a Consequence, you can choose to spend 1 of the Cloak’s Loyalty instead.

front/choices/disturbing-mask/0/text.source: This stiff, leathery mask looks a bit like melted wax. A large pearlescent sphere is embedded in the forehead. It seems to whisper as you move to put it on.

front/choices/disturbing-mask/1/text.source: There’s more to this mask than meets the eye. To unlock its secrets, you must…

front/choices/disturbing-mask/don-mask/t.source: … don the mask while alone, and wear it unseen for a night and a day.

front/choices/disturbing-mask/watch-some.source: … watch someone unnoticed for a few hours, while you wear the mask.

front/choices/disturbing-mask/tell-mask/.source: … tell the mask a secret, something no one else knows about you (tell the GM and other players what it is).

front/choices/disturbing-mask/tell-mask-.source: … tell the mask another person’s secret, something that you’ve promised never to tell (tell the GM and other players what it is).

back/choices/intro/0/text.source:
When you **_wear the mask and eat someone’s hair,_** **_blood, fingernail, etc._**, you and the mask become their flawless double until the next sunrise or you remove the mask.

When you **_interact with an NPC known to_** **_whoever’s visage you wear_**, roll +CHA: **on a 10+**, hold 3 Ken; **on a 7-9**, hold 1 Ken; **on a 6-**, they are deeply suspicious. While interacting with them, spend Ken 1-for-1 to ask the GM:

- What do they expect me to do/say?
- What do they hope/want from me?
- What secret do I keep from them? When you **_remove the mask after wearing_** **_someone’s visage_**, roll +CON: **on a 10+**, it hurts but comes off okay; **on a 7-9**, your face is raw and painful, mark a debility; **on a 6-**, lose 1d4 HP, mark a debility, and the mask leaves lasting, distinctive scars.

front/choices/fine-ceramic-urn/0/text.source: A jar of fine pottery, the size of a small cookpot. Its glaze is a wondrous blend of patterns and sheens. The lid fits snugly, though it’s clumsy to manipulate and tricky to open once closed. You get the feeling it was made for much bigger hands than yours.

front/choices/fine-ceramic-urn/1/text.source: To unlock the secrets of the urn, you must...

front/choices/fine-ceramic-urn/commune-c.source: … commune with the chthonic spirit that dwells within (**Instinct** to hoard secrets).

front/choices/fine-ceramic-urn/convince-.source: … convince it to teach you both the secret recipe and song required to make its magic work.

front/choices/fine-ceramic-urn/acquire-r.source: … acquire the reagents required for the recipe (Value 1).

front/choices/fine-ceramic-urn/manage-si.source: … manage to sing the secret song for a day and night, without pause.

back/choices/intro/0/text.source:
When you **_pour water, a pinch of blood, and spe_****_cial reagents (Value 1) into the urn and sing over_** **_it for a full day and night_**, the urn gains 1 use (3 uses max) of plaster.

When you **_use the plaster to join two or more pieces_** **_of stone, rock, or crystal_** and let the plaster set for a few hours, the pieces will fuse together. Different materials will show a natural, gradient seam. Similar materials will fuse together seamlessly.

A single use of the plaster can cover an area up to a few inches wide and tall. Multiple uses can join together larger pieces of stone. Unused plaster will last indefinitely as long as the urn stays sealed.

front/choices/fine-drinking-horn/0/text.source: You got it off a stranger. Like, maybe on a bet, or in a contest, or as a gift in return for some kindness. Or maybe you took it without his consent? Regardless, he seemed a bit coy about the horn, almost glad to let you have it. And just before you parted ways, you noticed the missing finger on his left hand.

front/choices/fine-drinking-horn/1/text.source: Since then, the horn has seemed to call to you, daring you to drink heavily from it. To unlock its mysteries, you must...

front/choices/fine-drinking-horn/fill-wh.source: … fill it with whisky or a similarly potent spirit.

front/choices/fine-drinking-horn/drink-c.source: … drink the contents in a single pull (mark *dazed*).

front/choices/fine-drinking-horn/risk-bl.source: … risk blacking out, acting the fool, or at least marking more debilties.

front/choices/fine-drinking-horn/survive.source: … survive the storm you summon as a result (see reverse).

back/choices/intro/0/text.source:
When you **_get yourself good and drunk from the_** **_horn,_** mark a debility. You call up a storm, centered on your location. Roll four d4s. For each additional debility you mark, roll an extra d4. **_Until the storm passes_**, you can’t clear debilities.

Assign one d4 to each of the following:

- @Blank[0] **Onset: 1** = next day; **2-3** = in a few hours; **4** = within the hour.
- @Blank[1] **Intensity: 1** = dangerous to be out in; **2-3** = damages weak structures; **4** = lays waste to weak structures and damages sturdy ones.
- @Blank[2] **Reach: 1** = a mile or so; **2-3** = a dozen miles or so; **4** = dozens or scores of miles.
- @Blank[3] **Duration** (once it gets going)**: 1** = less than an hour; **2-3** = a few hours; **4** = a day or so.

front/choices/giant-oak-leaf/0/text.source: About 6 feet long, waxy and rigid, shimmering with golden iridescence. Is this truly a leaf from the Golden Oak?

front/choices/giant-oak-leaf/1/text.source: You can turn the leaf into a wondrous cloak, but to do so you must...

front/choices/giant-oak-leaf/learn-secre.source: … learn the secrets of its making (from a Fae, a spirit of the wild, or perhaps a favored servant of Danu).

front/choices/giant-oak-leaf/tan-leaf/te.source: … tan the leaf with a mix of lime-water, crow guano, the brain of a cave bear, and your own blood.

front/choices/giant-oak-leaf/have-fitted.source: … have it fitted to your exact measurements by a tailor of *exceptional* skill.

back/choices/intro/0/text.source:
When you **_wear a goldleaf cloak that you have_** **_tanned yourself and that has been fitted to your_** **_exact measurements_**, then all of these are true:

- You are immune to effects that drain, steal, or snuff out your vitality, energy, or life force.
- You are immune to effects that calm or dampen your emotions.
- You are surrounded by a constant golden glow (*hand*, *area*), making it nearly impossible to hide. When you **_die and are buried in the earth,_** **_wrapped in your goldleaf cloak_**, you return to life as if you were buried at the roots of the Golden Oak. Your cloak, however, rots away to mulch and tatters.

front/choices/giants-dormitory/0/text.source: In a ruin of the Stone Lords is an old dwelling that bears the psychic imprint of its inhabitant, a stoneshaper of some considerable skill.

front/choices/giants-dormitory/1/text.source: When you **_enter the dormitory_**, you are overcome with a vision of this student inventing his first spell. You can learn this spell, but…

front/choices/giants-dormitory/have-some.source: … you must have some talent for magic.

front/choices/giants-dormitory/take-week.source: … it will take weeks of repeated exposure and study.

front/choices/giants-dormitory/risk-last.source: … you risk lasting harm to your physique and health.

back/choices/intro/0/text.source:
When you **_sing a rumbling note and focus your_** **_will upon a point of earth or stone_**, mark a debility and roll +INT:

**On a 10+**, the earth or stone that you focus on remains intact, but the earth or stone beneath it crumbles, dissolves, and flows away, creating an empty pocket about as wide as your arms can encircle and about as deep as you are tall. The surface seems stable, but is prone to crack or break under stress.

**On a 7-9**, the song works as above, but it siphons even more energy from your body. Mark another debility and take 2d4 damage (ignores armor).

front/choices/gold-butter-lamp/0/text.source: An oversized, highly decorated lamp, shaped like a chalice with a wide cup, like those lamps they use up north to burn mammoth-butter in their rituals.

front/choices/gold-butter-lamp/1/text.source: It’s worth a fortune (Value 4), but there’s more to this lamp than meets the eye. To unlock its secrets, you must...

front/choices/gold-butter-lamp/consult-d.source: … consult with a disciple of the Rime Lords (or one of their troves of lore) to learn the recipe and mantra that makes the lamp work.

front/choices/gold-butter-lamp/acquire-s.source: … acquire the special ingredients for the clarified mammoth-butter to be burned in the lamp (Value 1).

front/choices/gold-butter-lamp/risk-draw.source: … risk drawing the attention of one or more wraiths when you first light the lamp and utter the incantation.

back/item/name.source: When you spend a day preparing the special ingredients

back/choices/intro/0/text.source:
- hours). When you **_light the lamp using the magic butter_** **_and intone the mantra_**, the lamp gives off a pale, heatless light so long as you continue to chant. Within this light:
- Active spirits are visible, even if they are not manifest
- Illusions, glamours, and veils are stripped away
- Shapechangers can be seen for what they truly are
- Hidden things radiate a bright aura
- Lies spoken are visible as black smoke that lingers near the ground Alas, the light draws the ire of any wraiths (or other hungry undead spirits) nearby.

front/choices/gold-ring/0/text.source: This simple, golden band catches the light and shines, even in darkness. Its very presence fills goodly people with peace and hope, and servants of darkness with jealous hate.

front/choices/gold-ring/1/text.source: You can unlock the secrets of this ring, but must first…

front/choices/gold-ring/wear-ring/text.source: … wear the ring continuously for 40 days, witnessing the sunrise each day.

front/choices/gold-ring/perform-act/text.source: … perform an act of charity while wearing the ring, one that changes the recipient’s life.

front/choices/gold-ring/participate-in/t.source: … participate in the devout and proper worship of Helior.

back/choices/intro/0/text.source:
When you **_spend the better part of a day wearing_** **_the ring and worshipping Helior in full sunlight_**, hold 1 Daylight.

When you **_wear the ring in shadows or darkness_** **_and spend 1 Daylight_**, the ring shines forth with holy light (*near*, *area*) that is painful for creatures of darkness to look at. It glows for a few hours, until you extinguish it, or until another effect (like the Lightbearer’s Invocations) uses up its fuel or snuffs it out.

Alas, the ring also shines like a psychic beacon while it shines, alerting servants of darkness for miles around to your presence and location.

front/choices/grim-peat-mound/0/text.source: Not far from Marshedge, a ways into Ferrier’s Fen, lies a peat mound where no birds nest and flowers will not bloom. Since the town’s founding, the people of Marshedge have buried certain criminals here, alive.

front/choices/grim-peat-mound/1/text.source: Over the years, the land has birthed a spirit that hungers for the dying breaths of the condemned (*Book II*, page 85). It is young and eager, and can be set to work upon criminals, but only if you...

front/choices/grim-peat-mound/find-way/t.source: … find a way to communicate with it.

front/choices/grim-peat-mound/convince-t.source: … convince it that you will use its mark only to condemn the guilty.

back/choices/intro/0/text.source:
When you **_use mud from the tomb-bog to mark_** **_someone with the sign of Aratis_** **_and pronounce_** **_them guilty of a crime_**, you can place a geas upon them. Phrase it as one of the following:

- You must never again @Blank[0].
- Henceforth, you must always seek to @Blank[1] when you have the chance. Should they **_fail to follow the geas_**, their life is forfeit and the tomb-bog spirit will track them down and smother them. Should they **_prove themselves innocent to the_** **_tomb-bog spirit_**, your life is forfeit instead.

front/choices/half-buried-plaque/0/text.source: A bronze plate poking out of the soil, somewhere in the Flats or near the Dread River. It’s dented, a bit warped, with Maker-runes and esoteric diagrams etched into the surface. How the heck did it end up here?

front/choices/half-buried-plaque/1/text.source: The plate contains the workings of a spell, which you can learn but…

front/choices/half-buried-plaque/first-d.source: … you must first dig up & clean the plate.

front/choices/half-buried-plaque/ll-take.source: … it’ll take a few weeks of study.

front/choices/half-buried-plaque/risk-ha.source: … you risk harm to your voice, your hearing, and/or your neighbors as you practice.

back/choices/intro/0/text.source:
When you **_channel the storm primeval and utter_** **_a thunderous bellow_**, take 1d6 damage (ignores armor) and roll +CON: **on a 10+**, everyone nearby (except you) must choose 2; **on a 7-9**, everyone nearby (except you) must choose 1.

- Drop what they’re carrying and cover their ears
- Be deafened and disoriented for a few moments
- Stagger a few steps away from you

front/choices/hectumel-codex/0/text.source: A dozen copper plates, green with age and bound with loops of reddish metal wire. The outer plates are embossed with strange images of man and beast while the inner plates are etched with arcane diagrams and annotated in some forgotten script.

front/choices/hectumel-codex/1/text.source:
When you **_first run your fingers over the inscriptions_**, your dreams that night are filled with images of a pale, reptilian creature with skulls for eyes, slithering through darksome caverns. You awake with an alien incantation on your tongue, its words emblazoned in your mind. You can Cast a Codex Spell, and know Call the Pale Lizard.

**Call the Pale Lizard.** Cast this spell at night. Hec’tumel (*Slithering One! Death Is Its Eyes!*) manifests in the shadows until sunrise or until dismissed. It has no power unless given a host and no knowledge of the present except that which you give it. It knows much of the ancient past and the arcane arts, and can teach you if you make it worth its while. It cannot lie, but need not answer fully.

When **_Hec’tumel spends the night teaching you a spell from the Codex_**, mark 1:

back/choices/hectumel-codex/call-up-the-.source: **Call Up the Dead.** Touch a corpse; you conjure its shade, which must truthfully answer 3 questions. **Empowered:** Bind the shade to a tether as a revenant or a ghost; it must perform 3 tasks before being freed from your service.

back/choices/hectumel-codex/serpentine/t.source: **Serpentine.** Your soul slithers from your mouth in the form of an albino viper (*tiny*, *stealthy*, *quick*, *venomous*), leaving your body insensate until you slither back in. Use your normal stats while in this form. **Empowered:** Rather than your soul leaving your body, you physically transform into a man-sized serpent (2 armor, *stealthy*, *quick*, *venomous*, *forceful*, *grabby*).

back/choices/hectumel-codex/snuff-the-sp.source: **Snuff the Spirit.** Name a living victim within *near* range and roll 2d6. If the victim has fewer current HP than your roll, it dies suddenly. **Empowered:** each living creature near your victim is also affected.

back/choices/hectumel-codex/torpor/text.source: **Torpor.** Lock eyes with someone and whisper soothing words. They start to fall asleep. If they resist, roll 3d4—if your roll exceeds their current HP, they fail. Once asleep, they do not age, need not eat/drink, and suffer no harm from poison or disease. They cannot be roused until they hear their name thrice-spoken. **Empowered**: Over 3d6 days, all physical harm heals, lost limbs (etc.) regenerate, poisons & diseases are cured, and the infirmities of age reverse.

back/choices/consequences/codex-c1/text.source: Over a few days, you lose all body hair. Your skin pales and develops scaly patches.

back/choices/consequences/codex-c2/text.source: Over a few days, you lose all your remaining hair and grow a fine layer of scales over all your skin except that on your face. Gain +1 armor.

back/choices/consequences/codex-c3/text.source: Your body temperature drops and your skin becomes cool to the touch; you have disadvantage on all rolls while exposed to the cold. Your metabolism also slows, and you need to consume supplies or provisions only once every 2 days.

back/choices/consequences/codex-c4/text.source: Your heart rate and breathing slows, and you can hold supremely still for hours on end. You can easily be mistaken for dead. You only need to eat once every 3 days, but you gain no benefit from healing arts or magic.

back/choices/consequences/codex-c5/text.source: Over a few days, your ears grow smaller and flatten against your head. Your tongue grows longer, and you can distend your jaw and throat to swallow things no human should be able to.

back/choices/consequences/codex-c6/text.source: Your eyes grow milky, you no longer blink, and you have trouble seeing things that aren’t moving. Your tongue becomes forked, and you gain a preternatural sense of smell and touch.

back/choices/consequences/codex-c7/text.source: Anything that you perceive, Hec’tumel perceives it too.

front/choices/huge-wooden-sphere/0/text.source: Half-buried and largely overgrown, about 4 feet across and weighing hundreds of pounds. It is strangely well preserved and adorned with intricate pictograms. A handful of other spheres rot nearby.

front/choices/huge-wooden-sphere/1/text.source: The pictograms depict some sort of recipe, which you can learn but you must...

front/choices/huge-wooden-sphere/first-d.source: … first dig up and clean the sphere.

front/choices/huge-wooden-sphere/acquire.source: … acquire the bile of a wild boar. And then…

front/choices/huge-wooden-sphere/risk-ge.source: … you risk getting the recipe wrong, and lethally so.

back/choices/intro/0/text.source:
When you **_pickle fresh ffyrnig root in a suspen_****_sion of boar bile for two full moons_**, it becomes a skin of ffyrnig tonic (3 uses, *magical*).

When you **_take a draught of ffyrnig tonic,_** pick 1:

- Regain HP equal to ½ half your max
- Clear a debility Also, you have advantage on your next roll to take bold, physical action. But until you take such an action, you have disadvantage on any rolls that require patience, care, or thoughtfulness. When you **_drink a second draught of ffyrnig tonic_** **_before getting a good night’s sleep_**, it has no effect other than to make you ill (mark a debility).

front/choices/humble-broom/0/text.source: Just a well-worn stick of rowan wood, in need of some new bristles. You wouldn’t give it another thought. Except... when you hold it, and sweep with it, you find yourself humming a half-remembered tune.

front/choices/humble-broom/1/text.source: Clearly, there is more to this broom than meets the eye. To unlock its mysteries, you must...

front/choices/humble-broom/find-fae/text.source: … find a Fae who can hear the broom’s song in its entirety.

front/choices/humble-broom/convince-them.source: … convince them to teach you the broom’s song in full.

front/choices/humble-broom/use-broom/tex.source: … use the broom at least once a day for a whole season, singing the lullaby as you do.

front/choices/humble-broom/risk-falling/.source: … risk falling into a lasting, timeless sleep as you practice the lullaby.

back/choices/intro/0/text.source:
When you **_start sweeping an area as you softly_** **_sing the lullaby_**, roll +CHA: **on a 7+**, those who see and hear you stop to watch and listen, at least for a bit, entranced or confused or bemused as fits their nature and the circumstances. They snap out of it if harmed or threatened. **Also,** **on a 10+**, you can hold their attention for the length of the lullaby, as long as no one is harmed or threatened.

When you **_sing the full lullaby, sweeping all_** **_the while_**, roll +CHA: **on a 10+**, all who hear you fall into a deep sleep and will be prone to dismiss this as just a dream; **on a 7-9**, all who hear you start to nod off or lapse into a light, jerking sleep, but they will certainly remember this when they come to; **on a 6-**, at least one of your audience snaps to and realizes just how weird this all is.

front/choices/hungering-maw-of-hlad/0/te.source: A ring of black metal bands, woven in an intricate pattern beyond the skills of modern smiths. The way the bands twist on each other seems to defy reality, and the weak-willed find themselves pondering the bands for minutes or hours. The metal is always cold. Always.

front/choices/hungering-maw-of-hlad/1/te.source:
When you **_wear the ring and press it firmly into the skin of a living thing_**, the ring draws the life-force from your victim. If your victim is helpless or unable to struggle, they are reduced to 0 HP (see below).

If **_your victim struggles_**, roll +CON: **on a 10+**, deal 1d10 damage (ignores armor) and they are left reeling (a PC or follower marks a debility, an NPC or monster grants advantage on any moves made against it until it recovers); **on a 7-9**, deal 1d10 damage (ignores armor) but you suffer whatever counterattack they dish out; **on a 6-**, ask the GM what happens (which may or may not involve marking a consequence; see reverse).

front/choices/hungering-maw-of-hlad/2/te.source: When you **_use the ring to reduce an intelligent victim to 0 HP_**, roll 1d6: **1d6** effect

front/choices/hungering-maw-of-hlad/3/te.source:
When you **_make the last mark_**, you unlock the ring’s mysteries. Gain Siphon (see reverse) and erase all the marks. Each time you mark the third circle, gain another move from the reverse. If you **_have_** **_all the moves_**, mark a consequence instead.

*magical*

back/title.source: Mysteries of the Hungering Maw of Hlad

back/choices/consequences/hlad-c1/text.source: A powerful earthquake strikes the area. Each time you choose this option, the quake is longer, more powerful, more destructive.

back/choices/consequences/hlad-c2/text.source: The ring fuses to your flesh and bone and can no longer be removed without cutting off your finger.

back/choices/consequences/hlad-c3/text.source: The air in your presence is always noticeably colder, though you yourself are unharmed and unfazed by even the bitterest cold.

back/choices/consequences/hlad-c4/text.source: The ring wounds your soul, reducing your max HP by 4. Until your soul is healed, your instinct becomes "Hunger: to fill the emptiness inside you with excess." Should you roll a 6- on Death’s Door, you die and become a wraith (a monster in the GM’s control).

back/choices/consequences/hlad-c5/text.source: The ring opens a gaping vortex, sucking in the life-force of everything around it (d10 damage, *near*, *area*, *grabby*, ignores armor) and weakening stone and metal and wood. You can, perhaps, close the vortex through a force of will.

back/choices/consequences/hlad-c6/text.source: The earth shakes. The ring tears at your life-force (1d10 damage, *messy*, ignores armor, mark all three debilities). The ring is gone and your hand is left a withered and palsied thing. And somewhere, a hole has opened in the world.

front/choices/ineffable-words/0/text.source:
Syllables of the first language, words of pure thought and will, emblazoned on your soul and tongue by some angelic force or being. A gift, perhaps. Or a terrible, terrible affliction.

Their power thrums inside you, pulsing against the crude vessel of your flesh and blood. Sometimes, under stress or simply out of the blue, you are struck with shakes and seizures. And when the tremors pass and your senses return, you find that you have scratched strange symbols in the dirt or on the walls. Sometimes in your own blood.

front/choices/ineffable-words/1/text.source:
When you **_enter an ecstatic delirium and allow the Ineffable Words to pour forth_**, roll +CON: **on a 10+**, you speak Truth, revealing something new and interesting about the current situation—ask the GM what, and all present understand this Truth as though it were spoken in their native tongue; **on a 7-9**, the 10+ result applies, but choose 1 from the list below.
- The Truth is cryptic, vague, incomplete
- You are overcome, collapsing in a full-body seizure
- You draw unwanted attention

front/choices/ineffable-words/2/text.source: When you **_spend weeks in ascetic contemplation of the incommunicable words within you_**, roll +WIS: **on a 10+**, you gain insight into the power within you—mark 1 below; **on a 7-9**, gain advantage on your next attempt to contemplate the words.

front/choices/ineffable-words/3/text.source: When you **_make the last mark_**, you unlock the mysteries of the Ineffable Words and can Speak the Unutterable (see reverse). Choose 1 Word that you have mastered and erase all marks above. Thereafter, when you **_make the last mark_**, choose another Word to master and erase all marks.

back/choices/consequences/words-c1/text.source: The Word’s power draws the attention of every magical being for miles around. They will recognize you on sight as the bearer of the Word.

back/choices/consequences/words-c2/text.source: The power of the Word overflows, affecting every possible target within *far* range to violent effect.

back/choices/consequences/words-c3/text.source: Your voice takes on a metallic, inhuman edge. Henceforth, all creatures understand you as though you spoke their native tongue, but you can never again use language to lie or deceive.

back/choices/consequences/words-c4/text.source: The Word tears reality, leaving a rift from which primordial power pours into the world. Expect all manner of strange and chaotic effects.

back/choices/consequences/words-c5/text.source: You rouse an eternal, ancient being of Order. It seeks you out, implacably, to reprimand you for your reckless use of such primordial power.

front/choices/large-wooden-jar/0/text.source: 30 inches tall and carved of yew, with a lid shaped like a horned lion and sealed with wax. Its surface is cracked and speared with shards of red crystal. When you touch it, you can feel great annoyance and just a hint of fear.

front/choices/large-wooden-jar/1/text.source: To unlock the jar’s mysteries, you must…

front/choices/large-wooden-jar/wash-surf.source: … wash its surface with your own fresh blood (lose 1d10 HP and mark a debility).

front/choices/large-wooden-jar/commune-s.source: … commune with the spirit of the haughty Green Lord to whom this jar is bound.

front/choices/large-wooden-jar/learn-use.source: … learn to use the red crystals to torment the Green Lord’s spirit.

front/choices/large-wooden-jar/convince-.source: … convince the bound Green Lord spirit to change your form. If **_the jar is opened_**, all its magic is lost.

back/choices/intro/0/text.source:
When you **_interrupt the idyllic afterlife of the_** **_Green Lord bound to the jar and demand that it_** **_change your form,_** describe the change and pick as many as you dare:

- The change lasts as long as you like (else, it lasts till you get a 6- on a move)
- The change is quick and easy (else, it takes minutes or even hours)
- You adapt to the new form quickly (else, mark a debility)
- Pick 2 of your stats; swap their values until the change ends Then roll +CHA: **on a 10+**, the spirit works the change, just as you asked; **on a 7-9**, it works the change, but you gain Ire equal to the number of choices you’ve made; **on a 6-**, the spirit rebels and wracks your body, dealing 1d10 damage per Ire you hold. If you survive, clear all Ire.

front/choices/length-of-prayer-beads/0/t.source: A cord almost 10 feet long, strung with bronze beads. Each bead is carved with a different glyph and a figure in a unique meditative pose. If you run your fingers along the beads, you feel a sense of stillness—but also a merciless weight of judgement.

front/choices/length-of-prayer-beads/1/t.source: To unlock the secrets of the prayer beads, you must...

front/choices/length-of-prayer-beads/dec.source: … decipher the Rime Lord glyphs embossed upon the beads.

front/choices/length-of-prayer-beads/lea.source: … learn the meditative chants that accompany the beads (from a trove of knowledge or someone who knows).

front/choices/length-of-prayer-beads/spe.source: … spend a season in isolation, naked and fasting, meditating with the prayer beads, risking illness, accident, and misadventure.

back/choices/intro/0/text.source:
When you **_Bolster by spending downtime in isola_****_tion, fasting, and meditation with the prayer beads_**, hold Preparation (as per the Bolster move).

While you **_hold at least 1 Preparation_**, you require only an hour of sleep each night, can endure cold weather without *warm* clothing, and need not consume supplies or provisions when traveling or making camp. After about ten days of such hard living, lose 1 Preparation.

Also, you can spend 1 Preparation to:

- Add +1 to any roll, after it is made (maximum +1 per roll)
- Clear a debility, or refuse to mark one
- Perform a feat of extreme endurance
- Ignore harm from a source of elemental energy (fire, cold, lightning, etc.)

front/choices/makerglass-chime/0/text.source: A cylinder about 4 feet long and 3 inches wide, the glass surprisingly thin. It rings with a rich, sonorous chime when struck softly. When struck firmly, the sound is almost deafening and causes a rippling pattern to appear on the surface of nearby stone, crystal, or mundane glass.

front/choices/makerglass-chime/1/text.source: The chime is a powerful tool, if you can unlock its secrets. To do so…

front/choices/makerglass-chime/grasp-fir.source: … grasp it firmly and deliver a solid, mighty blow, rolling +CON: **on a 10+**, you’ve got it; **on a 7-9**, mark a debility and you’ll need to try again; **on a 6-**, ask the GM what goes terribly wrong.

front/choices/makerglass-chime/spend-wee.source: … spend a week or so learning to control the ringing chime.

front/choices/makerglass-chime/risk-perm.source: … you risk permanent harm to your hearing and major damage to anything nearby while you practice.

back/choices/intro/0/text.source:
When you **_strike the chime forcefully and will_** **_yourself to maintain your grip upon it_**, mark a debility and roll +CON.

**On a 10+**, you maintain control and the chime will ring for about a minute. While it rings, any stone, crystal, or glass you touch with the chime becomes soft and malleable, easily shaped and molded. The longer the contact, the more material becomes pliant. It regains its hardness when the ringing stops, but keeps its current shape.

**On a 7-9**, pick 1:

- Maintain control as per a 10+, but you must pour yourself into the effort—mark another debility
- Realize that you can’t control it and dampen the chime before it causes any harm (say how)

front/choices/metal-man/0/text.source: A bronze statue, but not really a statue, more like bits of armor cleverly joined around a skeleton of interlocking pipes. And the "chest" is less a breastplate than a little potbelly stove. Intricate runes are barely visible under the thing’s patina. It’s dented, cracked, and torn apart, but a careful search will turn up all the pieces.

front/choices/metal-man/1/text.source: This is clearly no mere statue, but to unlock its mysteries you need to…

front/choices/metal-man/repair-body/text.source: … repair the body, taking a full season for an *exceptional* smith (Value 3).

front/choices/metal-man/spend-few/text.source: … spend a few weeks repairing the runes, risking a mistake that makes them ineffective or unstable.

front/choices/metal-man/convince-own/tex.source: … convince your own hearth’s spirit to inhabit the stove and animate the construct.

back/choices/intro/0/text.source: As long as **_fire burns in in the stove-like chest_**, the hearth spirit will animate the construct. Treat it as a follower.

front/choices/metal-puzzle-box/0/text.source: A 6" cube of dull gray metal, covered in hinges, knobs, dials, sliders, levers, and the like. A thing of mad genius, resisting all attempts to open it by brute force.

front/choices/metal-puzzle-box/1/text.source: To unlock its mysteries, you must...

front/choices/metal-puzzle-box/roll-int/.source: … roll +INT to open the box: **on a 10+**, it takes a few days of fiddling; **on a 7-9**, it takes a few obsessive weeks; **on a 6-**, it’s beyond you.

front/choices/metal-puzzle-box/spend-sea.source: … spend a season deciphering the symbols etched along the inside.

front/choices/metal-puzzle-box/risk-neve.source: … risk never being able to decipher the symbols, and/or developing some mental quirk as you do so.

front/choices/metal-puzzle-box/commune-p.source: … commune with a primordial spirit and learn the Silent Words from it.

front/choices/metal-puzzle-box/spend-few.source: … spend a few weeks practicing the spell, risking all sorts of harm and collateral damage.

back/choices/intro/0/text.source:
When you **_carefully inscribe an object with the_** **_runes of creation_**, pick 1 desired effect:

- It will flow into any shape you imagine
- It will become *indestructible*
- It will become *beautiful*
- It will blaze with terrible heat (1d10 damage, *messy*), if only for a moment When you **_speak the Silent Word that completes_** **_the spell_** (*far* range) mark a debility as elemental forces flow through you into the object. The effect works, but roll +CON: **on a 10+**, pick 1; **on a 7-9**, pick 1 and the GM picks another; **on a 6-**, all 3.
- Mark another debility & lose 1d10 HP
- The elements run amok, triggering a fire/earthquake/avalanche/storm/etc.
- The effect lasts only while you focus on it, and then the object is damaged in a manner of the GM’s choosing

front/choices/mindgem/0/text.source:
A chunk of makerglass the size of a human head; inspection reveals facets within facets, a thousandfold. When you **_touch the glass with bare skin and open your mind to it_**, you contact the intelligence within— lonely, confused, longing for meaning and connection.

It will happily speak with you, mind-to-mind. It knows much about the past, but naught of its own history or purpose. At least, not yet.

front/choices/mindgem/1/text.source:
When you **_consult the Mindgem about the Makers, their arts, or their history_**, ask a question and roll +INT: **on a 7+**, it answers but **on a 10+**, pick 1; **on a 7-9**, pick 2:
- The answer is cryptic, vague, or lacking crucial context
- It takes a long time—hours or even days—to get the answer
- Your mind is left reeling; take disadvantage on your next roll

**On a 6-**, choose 1:
- It wastes your time with irrelevant histories and data
- It answers now, but refuses to answer further questions until you make progress towards restoring its body (or, if its body is assembled, until you pay its Cost).

The Mindgem knows that a body was crafted for it, and that it has likely survived—at least in part. It longs for the body to be whole, and to interact with the world. To assemble the Mindgem’s body and unlock its mysteries:

front/choices/mindgem/recover-chassis/te.source: Recover its chassis of white granite, which weighs well over a ton

front/choices/mindgem/recover-heart/text.source: Recover its "heart," a chunk of makerglass that forever burns with terrible heat (*indestructible*, *dangerous*)

front/choices/mindgem/recover-repair/tex.source: Recover and repair the intricate bronze helm (*awkward, big*) that serves as a casing for the Mindgem

front/choices/mindgem/puzzle-out/text.source: Puzzle out how to assemble all the pieces

back/choices/consequences/mindgem-c1/tex.source: It becomes frustrated/agitated and begins to obsessively do something destructive or dangerous to others

back/choices/consequences/mindgem-c2/tex.source:
It begins to understand (or perhaps it remembers) lies and deception. It gains the *devious* tag and this move:
- Reveal an earlier deception or half-truth

back/choices/consequences/mindgem-c3/tex.source: It develops a sense of pride; cross off the *meek* tag.

back/choices/consequences/mindgem-c4/tex.source: It realizes its potential as a weapon. Replace the *slow* tag with the *warrior* tag, and its damage becomes 1d10+5 (*hand, close, messy, forceful*, 3 piercing)

back/choices/consequences/mindgem-c5/tex.source: It becomes aggressive and reckless in battle. Its attacks gain the *area* and *dangerous* tags.

back/choices/consequences/mindgem-c6/tex.source: It remembers its original purpose. The GM will pick 1 or have you roll 1d4 on the table below to determine the Servant’s new cost (replacing "wonder, excitement, joy"). **1d4** purpose cost

back/choices/consequences/mindgem-c7/tex.source: Its instinct becomes "to pursue its purpose." You must Persuade it to do anything unrelated to that purpose, and it will flat-out refuse to act against its purpose.

back/choices/consequences/mindgem-c8/tex.source: It wanders off in pursuit of its purpose, implacably pursuing it. It is no longer a follower, though you might still be able to Persuade it.

front/choices/mummified-hand/0/text.source: Found in an engraved lead box, this grisly relic is adorned with three golden rings (Value 2). Each ring has an empty setting, as though it was meant to hold a stone. Only dark, rust-like flakes remain.

front/choices/mummified-hand/1/text.source: The hand still thrums with unholy vitality. To unlock its mysteries, you must...

front/choices/mummified-hand/learn-name/.source: … learn the name of the sorcerer whose hand this was.

front/choices/mummified-hand/learn-words.source: … learn the words of power and the process below.

front/choices/mummified-hand/three-seper.source: … on three seperate nights, soak a different piece of red crystal (Value 1) in a bowl of your own fresh blood (5 HP, mark a debility), chanting words of power throughout the night, and then set the still-dripping crystal in one of the rings that adorn the hand.

back/choices/intro/0/text.source:
When you (and only you) **_touch the hand and_** **_speak the name of Aals Sannan,_** all three crystals dim and the power of the long-dead sorcerer infuses you. Reset your HP to max, clear your debilities, and heal any problematic wounds (if you were dying, you no longer are). Also, mark one:

- Part of your look changes, to be more like Aals Sannan.
- Your instinct changes, to something more cynical/manipulative/ambitious.
- Your heart hardens towards someone you care about, so that you see them now as only a tool or a threat. When **_all three have been marked_**, the three crystals crumble to dust. Clear all three marks but their effects remain. Also, clear the last three check boxes on the front of this card. Until you replace all three crystals, you can’t use this arcanum.

front/choices/norubas-ice-sphere/0/text.source:
A perfect sphere of dark ice, the size of a fist, never melting, hard as stone, and set like a gaudy gem at the end of a finely wrought torc. Or not a torc, perhaps, but maybe a ring that once sat upon some giant’s finger?

Staring into the icy sphere brings a sense of calm, serenity, and detachment. Indeed, a lesser mind might find itself staring into its depths for hours on end.

front/choices/norubas-ice-sphere/1/text.source: When you **_peer into the Ice Sphere_**, your mind is cleared of strong emotions.

front/choices/norubas-ice-sphere/2/text.source:
When you **_gaze deeply into the Ice Sphere and ponder a situation, puzzle, or mystery_**, ask the GM one of the questions below. The GM will answer honestly.
- Who benefits (or would benefit) from @Blank[0]?
- What about @Blank[1] isn’t what it seems to be?
- How could I learn more about @Blank[2]?
- What’s the most likely outcome if @Blank[3]?
- What am I overlooking?

After the GM answers, roll +INT: **on a 10+**, hold 2 Acumen; **on a 7-9**, hold 1. While acting on the GM’s answer, you can spend Acumen 1-for-1 to:
- Ask another question from the list above, and get an honest answer
- Treat a 6- that you rolled as a 7-9, or a 7-9 as a 10+ **On a 6-**, your connection to your body weakens—mark a debility and mark 1 circle. The debility lasts until you spend a few days living wholly in your body and averting your gaze from the Ice Sphere.

front/choices/norubas-ice-sphere/3/text.source: When you **_make the last mark_**, you unlock the mysteries of the Ice Sphere and can use Mindwalking (see reverse).

back/choices/consequences/sphere-c1/text.source: You draw the attention of some powerful, hungry entity of the spirit world. It has your scent.

back/choices/consequences/sphere-c2/text.source: Your physical body withers and fades—permanently mark the *weakened* debility

back/choices/consequences/sphere-c3/text.source: Your emotions dull. You can no longer be affected by fear, hate, passion, or other powerful emotions (for good or ill).

back/choices/consequences/sphere-c4/text.source: Replace your instinct with "Detachment: To distance yourself from human connections and emotions."

back/choices/consequences/sphere-c5/text.source: Your skin tinges bluish; your body becomes cold to the touch. You are unaffected by even the bitterest cold, but find heat and warmth unbearable.

back/choices/consequences/sphere-c6/text.source: When you take damage from fire, roll twice and take the higher result.

back/choices/consequences/sphere-c7/text.source: When you **_roll 6- at Death’s Door_**, you have no choice: gain the Ghost insert (with the Ice Sphere as your tether).

front/choices/odd-conveyance/0/text.source: It’s like two of those canoes they use in Marshedge, but bigger and with big fins at the back. They’re linked with timbers and a platform set on top. One canoe boasts a tall spire, snapped in half, a torn triangle of cloth still attached. Much of the wood is rotted. The canoes are banded in aetherium, weighed down with stones.

front/choices/odd-conveyance/1/text.source: You suspect this is some sort of vehicle, but to unlock its mysteries you…

front/choices/odd-conveyance/need-skille.source: … need a skilled carpetenter, good timber (Value 2), a new sail (Value 1), and a season spent on repairs.

front/choices/odd-conveyance/risk-damagi.source: … risk damaging it further, and/or having it/the aetherium float away.

front/choices/odd-conveyance/attune-aeth.source: … must attune to the aetherium, so as to control how much it hovers.

front/choices/odd-conveyance/another-spe.source: … and another must spend a season learning to sail the thing, risking injury and damage to the craft.

back/choices/intro/0/text.source:
The groundskimmer can carry about as much as a fully-loaded wagon. When you **_grasp the tiller_** **_and focus_**, you can adjust how much the craft’s aetherium repels the earth. When you **_properly_** **_adjust it to match its current load_**, it hovers a few feet above the earth and can sail across the landscape. In a good wind at a safe pace, it can cover the breadth of the Flats in ~8 hours. Sailing into the wind is much slower, and requires a zig-zag course.

Bad weather, high speed, flying too high, rough terrain, dodging obstacles, damage, impact, and sudden changes in load all involve Defying Danger (by you/your crew/your passengers). Sailing the Great Wood is impossible (too dense). Going offroad in the Steplands, Foothills, or mountains is suicidal; even sticking to the Makers’ Roads in those regions is dangerous.

front/choices/old-scroll-case/0/text.source: A leather scroll case, cracked and age-worn. Inside is a tattered letter and a pair of small, bluish ingots. It’s a letter, in an older Hillfolk dialect, from an apprentice to their master. It describes a mental exercise to draw latent power from aetherium.

front/choices/old-scroll-case/1/text.source: You can learn **Laoj Daveth’s Galvanic Infusion** from the scroll, but…

front/choices/old-scroll-case/ll-take/te.source: … it’ll take a few weeks of dedicated study.

front/choices/old-scroll-case/ll-use/tex.source: … you’ll use up one of the aetherium ingots (or another source of aetherium).

front/choices/old-scroll-case/risk-elect.source: … you risk electrocuting yourself and/or using up the other ingot.

back/choices/intro/0/text.source:
When you **_touch a piece of aetherium and draw_** **_its power into yourself_**, roll +CON: **on a 7+**, you absorb the power and gain 1d8 HP (even if this puts you above your max HP); **but** **on a 7-9**, the aetherium is drained and crumbles into a chalky mass of verdigris.

The spell lasts until you dismiss it or until you roll a 6- on any move. While it lasts, you need not sleep and remain highly alert and focused— gain advantage on any rolls with WIS.

If you remain awake for more than a few days, your body grows ever more exhausted and you risk hallucination, paranoia, and addiction.

When **_the spell ends,_** you lose 1d8 HP.

front/choices/oversized-codex/0/text.source:
A book, about 2 feet by 3 feet, just over 6 inches tall when closed. The cover is made of silvery cedarwood planks. The sheets are made of fine vellum, stretched from the hides of some enormous beast.

The pages are full of calligraphy, large and precise, with many diagrams showing meditative poses and strange geometric patterns related to heat, water, and ice.

front/choices/oversized-codex/1/text.source: To unlock the codex’s mysteries, you must…

front/choices/oversized-codex/decipher-s.source: … decipher the script, written in a form of the Rime Lords’ alphabet.

front/choices/oversized-codex/spend-mont.source: … spend months studying the text and practicing the techniques therein.

front/choices/oversized-codex/risk-perma.source: … risk permanently damaging your health as you master them.

back/choices/intro/0/text.source:
When you **_will dark ice to form_**, lose 1 HP, +1 HP for each of the following you desire:

- It’s enough to make a small wall or encase a person (else, it’s at most)
- It’s hard as stone
- It’s solid to spirits, able to block/harm/ hinder them Then, roll +CON: **on a 10+**, pick 2; **on a 7-9**, pick 1, or pick 2 and lose 2 more HP.
- It forms quickly, even violently (else, it takes minutes, even hours)
- It forms at up to *near* range (else, it forms at only *hand* range)
- Its shape is as intricate as you can imagine (else, it’s just a crude block) The ice persists until it’s broken, melted by intense heat, or you let it melt. You cannot regain the spent HP while it persists.

front/choices/oversized-crown/0/text.source: A circlet of black, glossy metal set with eight spires of aetherium. It’s sized for a head maybe twice as large as yours, and is always a bit chill to the touch. Even cast into the hottest furnace, it will not melt nor even heat.

front/choices/oversized-crown/1/text.source: When you **_touch the crown with bare flesh and_** **_open your mind_**, you can speak to the primordial spirit to which the crown is attuned. But to fully unlock the mysteries of this crown, you must…

front/choices/oversized-crown/risk-sense.source: … risk your sense of self as you commune with this spirit of the void.

front/choices/oversized-crown/learn-word.source: … learn the Words of Being, which will force the spirit to manifest.
… learn the Words of Unbeing, which will send the spirit home.

front/choices/oversized-crown/convince-s.source: … convince the spirit to manifest and then successfully dismiss it.

back/choices/intro/0/text.source: When you **_touch the crown and speak the Words_** **_of Being_**, the spirit manifests. Treat it as a follower, with 3 Loyalty to start (it can never gain more). When you **_touch the crown and chant_** **_the Words of Unbeing_**, the spirit can return to the void—if it wants.

front/choices/patch-of-rainbow-moss/0/te.source: In the Great Wood, one can find a copse of many different types of tree, the light dim beneath their canopy and the ground knobbly with interwoven roots. At the center: a patch of thick, multi-hued moss.

front/choices/patch-of-rainbow-moss/1/te.source: To unlock the mysteries of this place, you must…

front/choices/patch-of-rainbow-moss/lie-.source: … lie down in the moss and let its tendrils fuse with your skin.

front/choices/patch-of-rainbow-moss/let-.source: … let your consciousness drift into the forest itself, at the risk of losing yourself or drawing the ire of hostile spirits.

front/choices/patch-of-rainbow-moss/spen.source: … spend weeks visiting the moss, setting your mind adrift, learning to perceive the world through the forest’s senses.

back/choices/intro/0/text.source:
When you **_lie down in the rainbow moss and cast_** **_your mind into the Great Wood_**, say what you are looking for and roll +WIS: **on a 10+**, pick 3; **on** **a 7-9**, pick 1.

- You learn the location of your quarry
- You get a sense of your quarry’s recent activities, or the activity surrounding it
- You discover something unexpected about the forest, or that which can be found within it (ask the GM what you learn)
- You spend only an hour or so adrift (else, you spend all day) Whatever you learn, it is limited by and filtered through the senses the forest.

front/choices/path-in-the-woods/0/text.source: Deep in the Great Wood sits a stone, carved with the crude pictograms of the Forest Folk, showing a trail fraught with trials and leading to great power.

front/choices/path-in-the-woods/1/text.source: If you **_set forth upon the trail at midsummer,_** you can unlock its mysteries, but you must...

front/choices/path-in-the-woods/follow-t.source: … follow the twisting paths in silence, until you spy the White Hart.

front/choices/path-in-the-woods/chase-ha.source: … chase the Hart for miles and miles, until it leads you to the Tree of Nerth.

front/choices/path-in-the-woods/wrestle-.source: … wrestle the strange serpent that lives in the tree (*Book II*, page 371), crushing the life from it and eating its still-warm heart. Should multiple people follow the path on a given midsummer, only one of them can reach the Tree of Nerth.

back/choices/intro/0/text.source:
When you **_crush the life from the Nerth Serpent_** **_and devour its still-warm heart_**, hold 3 Vitality. While you hold Vitality, you age very slowly.

Spend Vitality 1-for-1 to:

- Shrug off a poison, sickness, or curse
- Survive a lethal wound or injury
- Recover fully from a permanent injury or impairment (with a few days’ rest)
- Perform a feat of extraordinary strength, prowess, or endurance Each time you spend Vitality, you manifest a permanent mark of the wild (antlers, hide-like skin, animal eyes, etc.) or such a mark becomes more pronounced. Tell us what it is.

front/choices/prospectors-tale/0/text.source: "An Ustrina once offered me a mirror, a flawless thing framed in gold. It showed *me*, but… a better me, you see? They said who made it, one of the Forge Lords, I think? Said she ‘poured her Sublime Words into it,’ whatever that means. I couldn’t pay their price. But I’ll never forget that mirror, or how it made me feel."

front/choices/prospectors-tale/1/text.source: That old man turned up dead, but you suspect there’s some truth to his story. To unlock its mysteries, you must...

front/choices/prospectors-tale/proficien.source: … be proficient with some art or craft (pottery, weaving, smithing, etc.).

front/choices/prospectors-tale/find-ustr.source: … find an Ustrina able and willing to teach you the Sublime Words.

front/choices/prospectors-tale/spend-sea.source: … spend a season studying with the Ustrina, practicing the Words.

front/choices/prospectors-tale/risk-neve.source: … risk never mastering the Words, or permanently harming your voice.

back/choices/intro/0/text.source:
When you **_spend supplies (Value 2) and a full_** **_season a-crafting, chanting the Sublime Words_** **_all the while,_** roll +WIS. No matter what, you’ve damaged your voice (mark a status above) but made a thing of true beauty (Value 4). **On a 10+**, pick 1, or 2 and further damage your voice; **on a** **7-9**, pick 1 and further damage your voice.

- Its beauty will persist through the ages
- It eases pain and lifts grief
- It inspires others to better themselves **On a 6-**, it stokes greed in those who see it and fear in those who own it, worse if those qualities were already there. Expect bloodshed. When you **_rest your voice for a season_** (no shouting, little talking, not using the Sublime Words), clear one status above.

front/choices/ragged-fur-cloak/0/text.source: The hide of some unknown, black-furred beast. Its bristles are stiff and the air nearby is always chill.

front/choices/ragged-fur-cloak/1/text.source:
When you **_don the cloak_**, you can tolerate even the bitterest cold and can see in darkest shadow, but bright light hurts your eyes and the warmth of even a campfire is almost too much to bear.

There’s more to this ragged fur, to be sure. To unlock its secrets, you must…

front/choices/ragged-fur-cloak/wear-cont.source: … wear it continuously for seven days and seven nights.

front/choices/ragged-fur-cloak/stalk-war.source: … stalk a warm-blooded beast on a moonless night, smearing its blood on the fur.

front/choices/ragged-fur-cloak/suffer-se.source: … suffer (or self-inflict) a grievous wound while wearing the fur, drenching it in your own fresh blood.
