back/choices/intro/0/text.source:
When you **_open your own veins and drench the_** **_fur with your own fresh blood,_** lose 1d8 HP and mark a debility. If the cloak holds no Charges, it gains 1d4 Charges. The scars from the wound are bright white and never fade.

When you **_suffer a blow or physical injury while_** **_wearing the Darkwalker Cloak_**, it loses 1 Charge and you transform into a cloud of shadow. You suffer no harm after all and can flit and fly about for a few seconds before reforming. Everything you touch while in this shadowy form is laced with hoarfrost. This effect does not trigger if the fur has no Charges.

When **_direct sunlight or holy light touch the_** **_Darkwalker Cloak,_** or **_anyone but you dons it_**, it loses all its Charges.

front/choices/red-scepter/0/text.source: A bronze rod, tipped with a glowing red crystal and carved with openwork shapes of hungry, leering faces.

front/choices/red-scepter/1/text.source: When you **_hold the Scepter and wind blows through the openings in the crystal_**, it makes a soft howling noise.

front/choices/red-scepter/2/text.source: When you **_gesture at an open flame with the scepter_**, the flame flickers or flares as if blown by the wind.

front/choices/red-scepter/3/text.source: When you **_bleed a helpless, living creature and dip the Scepter’s crystal in their still-warm blood_**, mark 1 charge as the crystal soaks up the blood (to a maximum of 3):

front/choices/red-scepter/4/text.source: When you **_Inflame someone and they kill one or more living beings as a result_**, mark 1:

front/choices/red-scepter/5/text.source: When you **_make the last mark_**, you unlock the Scepter’s mysteries and gain Burning Hatred (see reverse).

back/choices/consequences/scepter-c1/tex.source: Your skin becomes feverish. You always feel hot and can’t bear to wear *warm* gear.

back/choices/consequences/scepter-c2/tex.source: Your eyes change, glowing like fiery embers. They flare with your temper.

back/choices/consequences/scepter-c3/tex.source: The crystal tip of the Scepter cracks, and you cannot use the Scepter’s powers until you have "fed" the Scepter another chunk of red crystal, one at least the size of your fist.

back/choices/consequences/scepter-c4/tex.source: To gain any future charge, the victim you bleed must be awake and terrified.

back/choices/consequences/scepter-c5/tex.source: To gain any future charge, the blood-letting must be brutal, messy, and wanton.

back/choices/consequences/scepter-c6/tex.source: Henceforth, when you **_incite someone to violence with the Scepter and they act as you suggest_**, they lose themselves to primal bloodlust. They feel no pain and revel in carnage until they are killed, restrained, or crippled.

back/choices/consequences/scepter-c7/tex.source: When you **_use Burning Hatred_**, something on your person or within reach also catches fire.

back/choices/consequences/scepter-c8/tex.source: You always hear a dim howling in the back of your mind. When the wind blows, the howling grows in volume, making it difficult to hear anything other than insults or plans to commit violence.

back/choices/consequences/scepter-c9/tex.source: When you **_Persuade using anything other than threats, pain, or violence_**, the best you can get is a 7-9.

front/choices/redwood-basin/0/text.source: A wide, shallow bowl carved with flowers and thorny vines, twining through skulls of deer and other beasts. The pattern shifts when you aren’t looking; it’s never exactly the same twice.

front/choices/redwood-basin/1/text.source: To unlock the mysteries of the basin, you must...

front/choices/redwood-basin/befriend-spi.source: … befriend the spirit of life and vitality that dwells within.

front/choices/redwood-basin/learn-fae/te.source: … learn from a Fae how to pour years of your life into the basin.

front/choices/redwood-basin/fill-basin/t.source: … fill the basin with a few years of your life. When you **_mark the last requirement and unlock_** **_this arcanum_**, mark your current age on the other side. Then trigger the Bittersweet Elixir move.

back/choices/intro/0/text.source:
When you **_fill the basin with a few years of your_** **_life_**, it becomes a draught of honey and regret. Either mark the next age above (and update your look) as the lost years catch up with you, or mark one of the following (your choice):

- Your mood shifts, dramatically (how?)
- You see the Last Door (what’s it like?)
- Reduce STR, DEX, or CON by 1
- You have less than a year to live When someone **_drinks down all of the bitter_****_sweet elixir, straight from the basin_**, they pick 1:
- Regain all HP, clear all debilities, and heal any active problematic wounds
- Purge themselves of all poison/disease
- Fully recover from a permanent injury by next season’s end, or sooner

front/choices/redwood-effigy/0/text.source: A vaguely man-shaped root of blood-red wood, wrapped in tattered cloth. Bright blue markings adorn the fabric, as do rust-colored stains. But you know that. After all, you made it yourself. You’ve bound your flesh and soul to the effigy, and this is the only one you will ever be able to make.

front/choices/redwood-effigy/1/text.source:
When you **_perform the secret rite_**, which requires privacy, a few hours, and a drop of your own fresh blood, hold 1 Conduit (max 1 Conduit, at least to start).

**SURROGATE SUFFERING** When you **_suffer physical harm while carrying the effigy on your person_**, you can spend 1 Conduit. If you do, the effigy suffers that harm in your place. You suffer no more than a passing inconvenience, and the effigy bears faint signs of the trauma it has endured in your stead.

Record the diverted harm on the image of the effigy above: a brief description of the injury, the HP that would have been lost, and any debilities you would have marked. Write small, in pencil. If the **_effigy is destroyed_**, you suffer all this harm at once.

**_Each time the effigy suffers harm on your behalf_**, mark 1. If all 3 marks are already marked, then mark a consequence instead (see reverse).

front/choices/redwood-effigy/2/text.source:
When you **_make the last mark_**, you unlock the effigy’s mysteries and gain Suffering Unleashed (see reverse).

*magical*

back/choices/consequences/effigy-c1/text.source: Your heartbeat slows and your emotions dull. Magic cannot stir your emotions unless it specifically targets the effigy. Alas, you can no longer Burn Brightly.

back/choices/consequences/effigy-c2/text.source: Your blood flows like sap and your muscles become like wood. Gain +1 armor and +4 max HP, but you can no longer regain HP via the Recover move. When you **_Make Camp_**, you must rest while touching soil or you get no benefit.

back/choices/consequences/effigy-c3/text.source: Henceforth, when **_anyone works magic upon the effigy_**, it affects you instead and bypasses any defenses that you have in place (including Surrogate Suffering).

back/choices/consequences/effigy-c4/text.source: Henceforth, when you **_suffer physical harm while you hold Conduit_**, you must spend it and use Surrogate Suffering.

back/choices/consequences/effigy-c5/text.source: The effigy becomes both *fragile* and highly flammable. When you suffer damage from heat or fire, you take +1d6 damage. If the effigy suffers harm from heat or fire in your place, it will burst into flames and be destroyed.

back/choices/consequences/effigy-c6/text.source: When you **_roll 6- at Death’s Door_**, you have no choice: gain the Revenant insert until the effigy is destroyed (and you become a wraith controlled by the GM) or it is buried in a Red Grove (and you become an NPC spirit of that grove). When you **_would mark a consequence but they’ve all been marked_**, pick a harm stored in the effigy at random. Erase that harm and suffer it now (it can’t be diverted).

front/choices/richly-woven-rug/0/text.source: About 4 feet by 7 feet unfurled, woven with stylized patterns of fire and flame. Flickering Maker-runes can be seen in the weaving, always out of focus but hinting at power.

front/choices/richly-woven-rug/1/text.source: You can unlock the secrets of this rug, but you must first…

front/choices/richly-woven-rug/marked-by.source: … be marked by fire, losing yourself to the panic or pain of burning.

front/choices/richly-woven-rug/then-spen.source: … then, spend weeks in meditation upon the rug and studying the now-clear runes.

front/choices/richly-woven-rug/allow-you.source: … allow yourself to be burned by a terrible flame, refusing to cry out and mastering your fear.

back/choices/intro/0/text.source:
When you **_spend an hour or so on the rug, med_****_itating on the fear of fire that all natural things_** **_possess_**, you hold Terror and mark 1 Heat.

- **Terror**: When you **_unleash the Terror_** **_you hold_**, all who see you fear you as they would fear the flame primeval, until you dismiss the effect. When you **_dismiss the effect_**, roll 1d6. If the roll is less than your Heat, then clear all your Heat and you painfully manifest a permanent sign of your connection to the flames: a blistered scar, reddish skin, glowing eyes, a sulfurous smell, etc. When **_a season passes without you unleashing_** **_Terror_**, reduce your Heat by 1.

front/choices/ring-of-daagon/0/text.source: A finely carved ring of copper, coated in verdigris and always a little damp. Its shape is that of a strange, reptilian creature devouring its own tail.

front/choices/ring-of-daagon/1/text.source: When you **_don the Ring_**, you feel the presence of every body of water within a few miles, natural or not, even if it is underground.

front/choices/ring-of-daagon/2/text.source: When you **_wear the Ring and caress its reptilian head_**, the air around you becomes damper and cooler. If you continue to caress it for a minute or so, a mist gathers near the ground and grows higher and thicker as long as you continue. A few minutes of caressing the Ring will blanket your immediate surroundings in thick, obscuring fog. Half an hour will blanket the countryside. The fog persists for as long as you caress the Ring, and then dissipates naturally based on the prevailing weather.

front/choices/ring-of-daagon/3/text.source: When you **_have used the Ring to summon an obscuring fog and a named creature dies within that fog_**, the Ring will ask you (silently, in your mind, not so much with words as with a deep longing) *May I* *take this one?* Should you assent, the creature’s body will be gone—vanished into the mists—as soon as no mortal is directly paying it heed. The first time this happens during each fog you summon, mark 1:

front/choices/ring-of-daagon/4/text.source: When you **_make the last mark_**, you unlock the ring’s mysteries and may Call Up the Deep Ones (see reverse) while wearing the ring. The ring itself becomes a follower.

back/title.source: Mysteries of the Ring of Daagon

back/choices/consequences/daagon-c1/text.source: Your skin becomes clammy and squamous.

back/choices/consequences/daagon-c2/text.source: You can breathe water through your skin, but must keep it moist or suffer increasing debilities.

back/choices/consequences/daagon-c3/text.source: You gain nourishment only from meat. Plants, grains and the like no longer count as supplies or provisions when you need to eat.

back/choices/consequences/daagon-c4/text.source: Only raw flesh nourishes you, but you are immune to food-borne illness.

back/choices/consequences/daagon-c5/text.source: 1d6 sinkholes appear within a few miles of you. At the bottom of each, a megalith protrudes from standing water, attended by servants of Daagon.

back/choices/consequences/daagon-c6/text.source: The ring’s Cost becomes "Living, helpless, intelligent sacrifices."

front/choices/rune-etched-pillars/0/text.source: Deep under a giant, ruined fort is a vaulted chamber, once a storeroom but looted long, long ago. A giant skeleton lies just inside, face-down, its skull and ribs staved in.

front/choices/rune-etched-pillars/1/text.source: Four pillars support the roof, carved with a series of huge runes that thrum with power. You can unlock their secrets, but…

front/choices/rune-etched-pillars/spend-.source: … you must spend a few days studying the runes and memorizing their sequence.

front/choices/rune-etched-pillars/medita.source: … you must meditate for a few weeks on the magic that infuses them.

front/choices/rune-etched-pillars/risk-t.source: … you risk triggering the spell contained in the runes, and collapsing the entire structure.

back/choices/intro/0/text.source:
When you **_carve the shattering words of Aalz_** **_Childric into stone or rock_**, designate a key word or phrase.

When you or another **_speaks the key word or_** **_phrase and wills the spell to trigger_**, you roll +CON: **on a 10+**, the rune-carved stone shatters and is immediately reduced to rubble; **on a 7-9**, the stone cracks and buckles, slowly breaking apart into a number of pieces.

front/choices/rune-laden-scales/0/text.source: An ancient vest of bluish steel, each scale etched with a silvery rune similar to those found among the ruins near Barrier Pass. A working of the Makers, no doubt, or at least of their most gifted students. The armor is surprisingly light and supple. The scales are always cold to the touch, and often edged in frost.

front/choices/rune-laden-scales/1/text.source: When you **_wear the Rune-laden Scales_**, you are perfectly comfortable in cold weather and suffer no harm from exposure or magic that might otherwise freeze your flesh. You have no such immunity to secondary effects of ice-magic, such as slipping, being impaled by an icicle, becoming encased in a block of ice, or the like.

front/choices/rune-laden-scales/2/text.source: When you **_wear the Rune-laden Scales and stand fast against a magical attack_**, roll +CON: **on a 10+**, the magic washes over you, unpleasant perhaps but with no ill effect; **on a 7-9**, you’re only partially affected—suffer half damage (if any) and a reduced effect; **on a 6-**, mark XP, and the magic affects you fully.

front/choices/rune-laden-scales/3/text.source: When you **_wear the Rune-laden Scales and defeat a wielder of chaotic magic_**, mark 1:

back/choices/consequences/scales-c1/text.source: You no longer mark 1 (see reverse) when you simply *defeat* a being that wields chaotic magic; you must destroy it instead.

back/choices/consequences/scales-c2/text.source: Mere minions and mindless horrors will no longer suffice. You only mark 1 for destroying a potent agent of chaos, such as a mighty demon or sorcerer.

back/choices/consequences/scales-c3/text.source: When you **_use or knowingly submit to chaotic magic_**, the Rune-laden Scales cease to benefit you or anyone you consider to be a friend or ally.

back/choices/consequences/scales-c4/text.source: When you **_kill a living creature out of anger, fear, or passion_**, even an agent of chaos, take disadvantage on all rolls until you ceremonially atone and purify yourself.

back/choices/consequences/scales-c5/text.source: When you **_take any violent action out of anger, fear, or passion_**, even against an agent of chaos, take disadvantage on all rolls until you ceremonially atone and purify yourself.

back/choices/consequences/scales-c6/text.source: You come to the attention of one of the mightiest of the Things Below, and they make your doom—or your corruption—a priority.

back/choices/consequences/scales-c7/text.source: You ascend into a vision state, in which you meet the spirit of the last hero to wear the Scales. Should you refuse the quest they offer, the Rune-laden Scales cease to function.

front/choices/runes-around-a-ruined-hall.source: In a ruined citadel of the Forge Lords, the grand hall lies empty. The throne is melted slag. The ceiling is shattered. The pillars are scorched and cracked. But intact around the outside of the room are a series of flowing runes. Close study reveals them to involve both fire and privacy.
The runes repeat themselves and can be copied, but...
… it takes a few hours of careful work.
… you risk a transcription error, but to what effect?

back/choices/intro/0/text.source:
When you **_precisely inscribe the flowing runes of_** **_the fiery veil along the outside of an area_**, the area is warded for as long as the runes remain intact.

When anyone **_tries to scry on the warded area_** **_from afar, or view it from the spirit realm_**, they see only a curtain of fire. If they insist on peering through the curtain, they are burned for 1d10 damage (advantage, ignores armor) and appear to those inside as a ghostly image wreathed in flames.

front/choices/runic-branding-iron/0/text.source: Found in the workshop of some Forge Lord, still held in a vice-clamp. The head is a runic shape, 6 by 6 inches, with smaller runes etched into its surface. Or at least, most of its surface. A few inches are blank, the work clearly unfinished.

front/choices/runic-branding-iron/1/text.source: To unlock the mysteries of this iron and claim its power as your own, you must...

front/choices/runic-branding-iron/deciph.source: … decipher the meaning of the runes, and identify the missing ones.

front/choices/runic-branding-iron/finish.source: … finish the etchings, risking an error that will make the next step fail.

front/choices/runic-branding-iron/heat-i.source: … heat the iron red-hot and let yourself be branded (lose 3d6 HP), the runes fading from the iron and searing themselves upon your soul.

front/choices/runic-branding-iron/allow-.source: … allow the wound to heal and scar, without the aid of any magic.

back/choices/intro/0/text.source:
When you **_call up the fire from your soul and_** **_pour it into your hands_**, roll +CON: **on a 7+**, your hands blaze like white-hot iron (see below); **but** **on a 10+**, first pick 1; **and on a 7-9**, first pick 2:

- It takes minutes of intense focus
- It burns your life force; lose 2d4 HP
- The pain is terrible; mark a debility **On a 6-**, whatever else the GM says, you cannot do this again until you Convalesce. While your **_hands are ablaze_**, your touch deals 1d10 damage (*hand*, *messy*, *dangerous*, 1 piercing), sets fire to wood, boils water, heats metal. Your hands are unharmed by the heat, but your gear and the rest of your body has no such protection. Be careful. Your hands blaze as long as you maintain your focus, up to a minute or maybe two.

front/choices/rusty-cauldron/0/text.source: Big enough for a grown man to crawl inside, pitted and scratched, engraved with whorly rune-like patterns. The whole thing is caked with rust. At least, you hope that’s rust.

front/choices/rusty-cauldron/1/text.source: The thing has a sinister feel, and you can sense its power. To unlock the cauldron’s mysteries, you must…

front/choices/rusty-cauldron/thoroughly-.source: … thoroughly scrub the rust from the cauldron.

front/choices/rusty-cauldron/spend-seven.source: … spend seven nights sleeping in the cauldron, dreaming foul dreams, marking a debility each time.

front/choices/rusty-cauldron/boil-bones/.source: … boil the bones of a beast that you honestly loved or valued, mixing in some of your fresh blood.

front/choices/rusty-cauldron/bring-wretc.source: … bring the wretched thing that arises under your control.

back/choices/intro/0/text.source:
When you **_boil the bones of beasts in the cauldron_** **_and stir in your own fresh blood,_** mark up to 3 debilities. An unliving chimera rises from the cauldron. Treat it as a follower, with a tag for each beast whose bones you used (*bear-like*, *owl-like*, etc.).

For each debility you marked, pick 1:

- It is stable (else, it falls apart in a day)
- It is not *clumsy*
- Replace its instinct with "to shun light"

front/choices/rusty-steel-blade/0/text.source: It was clearly once a fine, fine blade. The steel holds a pattern of rune-like sworls, at least where the rust hasn’t taken over. The hilt is blackened, with hints of leather wrappings that long ago burned away. The metal is hot to the touch, like it’s been left out for hours in the summer sun.

front/choices/rusty-steel-blade/1/text.source: To unlock the mysteries of this weapon, you must...

front/choices/rusty-steel-blade/restore-.source: … restore the blade, which requires access to a smithy, a few weeks of work, and no small amount of skill.

front/choices/rusty-steel-blade/commune-.source: … commune with the spirit of fire within the steel (**Instinct** to seek glory), and convince it that you are worthy to wield the blade.

front/choices/rusty-steel-blade/acquire-.source: … acquire a scabbard that can withstand the fire and heat of a forge.

back/choices/intro/0/text.source:
When you **_call on the fire spirit within,_** the blade erupts in flames (+*magical*, +*dangerous*) and casts light (*reach*, *area*). The hilt gets hot; wear thick gloves!

When you **_Clash with the Flaming Sword_**, after you resolve the move and deal damage, increase the Blaze die one step.

When you **_roll to make a move while wielding_** **_the sword_**, take damage equal to the Blaze die (ignores armor).

When you **_deal damage with the sword_**, add the Blaze die.

When you **_sheathe the sword_**, the fire goes out and cannot be relit until the Blaze die is nil. Reduce the Blaze die once each hour.

front/choices/scroll-and-bone-flute/0/te.source: A scroll, written in a cramped hand and seemingly nonsensical script, with a series of graph-like diagrams. It is accompanied by a flute of bone (from a human arm?). The notes reveal themselves to be a cipher; the graph is perhaps the notation for a song.

front/choices/scroll-and-bone-flute/1/te.source: You can unlock the secrets of the scroll and flute, but…

front/choices/scroll-and-bone-flute/firs.source: … you must first decipher the notes, which will take a few weeks of effort.
… the first time you use the flute, you risk getting the music wrong and aggravating the dool spirit.

back/choices/intro/0/text.source: When you **_stand among dool trees and play the_** **_proper tune on a flute of a murderer’s bone_**, you summon a dool spirit and bind it to your service. Treat it as a follower. Only one dool spirit will serve you at a time.

front/choices/sealed-cave/0/text.source: High in the hills or mountains, one can find a bricked-over cave mouth. Inside lie dozens of corpses, preserved for centuries by the cold. Many have malformations in the jaw, oversized teeth, elongated fingers that taper to claws. Few show signs of violence; they appear to have just laid down and died.

front/choices/sealed-cave/1/text.source: Indeed, the looping glyphs carved all over the cave walls sap your will to struggle, to fight, to do much of… anything. You can learn their mysteries, but…

front/choices/sealed-cave/ll-take/text.source: … it’ll take days of careful transcription, haunted by morose shades.

front/choices/sealed-cave/risk-succumbin.source: … you risk succumbing to the ennui of the place.

back/choices/intro/0/text.source:
When you **_mark a place with the peace-bond_** **_glyphs_**, violence (even to defend oneself) is suppressed in the area as long as the glyphs remain. The longer one stays in a peacebonded area, and the more tightly woven the glyphs are, the greater the effect.

When you **_attempt to commit violence within_** **_a peacebonded area, or to harm the peacebond_** **_glyphs themselves_**, you hesitate.

If you **_will yourself to continue_**, lose 1d4 HP and roll +WIS: **on a 10+**, go for it; **on a 7-9**, you act but have disadvantage on any rolls to commit violence (including damage); **on a 6-**, you fail to act and mark *dazed*.

front/choices/shield-of-the-wisent-witch.source:
+1 Readiness on a 7+ to Defend

A shield of horn-oak, glossy from long use, shod in bronze and adorned with a stylized wisent skull. It’s heavier than it looks, but its heft gives you a feeling of confidence, like anyone would be a fool to mess with a titan such as you.
When you **_bear the Shield openly_**, natural creatures give you wide berth and treat you with the respect that they would give a 1,000-lb. bison.

When you **_use the Shield to Defend with both feet planted firmly on the ground,_** so long as you hold Readiness you cannot be moved or tripped. When you **_spend Readiness to strike back at an attacker_**, you also break their momentum, knock them back, and/or send them reeling.
When you **_perform the sacred rites of the forest witches_**, alone in the woods under a clear crescent moon, mark 1:

back/title.source: Mysteries of the Shield of the Wisent Witch

back/choices/consequences/witch-c1/text.source: You give off a strong, musky scent no matter how much you bathe. It is distinctive and easily recognized.

back/choices/consequences/witch-c2/text.source: Over the next few days, you grow 4-6 inches.

back/choices/consequences/witch-c3/text.source: Over the next few days, your body mass doubles. Your size and relative strength remain mostly the same.

back/choices/consequences/witch-c4/text.source: You consume twice the normal amount of supplies or provisions each day.

back/choices/consequences/witch-c5/text.source: You make an inordinate amount of noise; your voice booms, your feet stomp heavily, even your breathing is loud.

back/choices/consequences/witch-c6/text.source: Your attacks all gain the *forceful* tag (and become more so if they already were *forceful*) and large weapons lose the *awkward* tag. Alas, you hardly know your own strength and must be careful to avoid breaking things (including your friends).

back/choices/consequences/witch-c7/text.source: Predators sense that you would be delicious and will choose to attack and eat you before just about any other potential prey.

back/choices/consequences/witch-c8/text.source: You become territorial and overly defensive of your allies. When someone or thing **_disrespects you,_** **_challenges your authority, or directly threatens your allies_**, you have disadvantage to do anything other than set them straight.

front/choices/silvery-glass-bottle/0/tex.source: About 10 inches tall, tapered at the top, made of old warped glass that’s shot through with silvery streaks, like the trails that slugs leave. The patterns in the glass seem different each time you look, almost shifting as you watch. It makes you eyes water, your head spin.

front/choices/silvery-glass-bottle/1/tex.source: You can unlock the secrets of this old glass bottle, but you must either…

front/choices/silvery-glass-bottle/find-.source: … find one who knows its workings, and get them to teach you; or…

front/choices/silvery-glass-bottle/fill-.source: … fill the botttle with spring-water and hallucinogenic mushrooms, and let it steep in the dark for a fortnight.

front/choices/silvery-glass-bottle/drink.source: … drink the contents and risk learning nothing as you suffer through the sickness and the nightmares.

back/choices/intro/0/text.source:
When you **_tie strands of someone’s hair around_** **_an item that they made or owned, set them afire,_** **_and drop them still-burning into the empty bottle,_** hold 3 Sway over them. The cinders continue to burn and glow until the Sway is gone. Spend 1 Sway while speaking their true name to…

- Twist their senses, making them perceive something untrue
- Plague them with nightmares until they wash in rain or snow
- Cause an emotion in their heart to swell, possibly overwhelming them If the person you currently hold Sway over finds and breaks the Witch Bottle, you will yourself suffer all the torments you have ever inflicted with it.

front/choices/silvery-signet-ring/0/text.source: A ring of white metal, untarnished and gleaming, a single glyph carved into the bezel. The symbol squirms under your gaze, like it exists in more dimensions than you can perceive. The ring fits you perfectly, of course.

front/choices/silvery-signet-ring/1/text.source: To unlock the ring’s mysteries, you must...

front/choices/silvery-signet-ring/spend-.source: … spend a season wearing the ring and contemplating the glyph.

front/choices/silvery-signet-ring/get-us.source: … get used to the headaches & nausea that come from wearing the ring.

front/choices/silvery-signet-ring/spend-.source: … spend 1 of your follower’s Loyalty to charge the ring.

front/choices/silvery-signet-ring/attemp.source: … attempt to influence one of your followers with the ring, at the risk of failing to ever master its power and/or alienating your follower(s).

back/choices/intro/0/text.source:
When you **_Strengthen Your Bond_** with a member of your community, you can choose to hold +1 Authority (max 3) in lieu of your follower holding +1 Loyalty. If you **_remove the ring_**, lose all Authority.

When you **_Persuade your follower(s) while hold_****_ing Authority_**, you have advantage.

You can spend Authority 1-for-1 to:

- Wrap yourself in majesty for up to a few minutes, drawing all attention, cowing the weak-willed, and speaking in a voice that all can hear (*far*, *area*)
- Will someone in your presence to do as you wish, attempting to Persuade them without words
- Have one of your nearby followers suffer an attack on your behalf, as if they held Readiness from Defending

front/choices/small-strange-book/0/text.source: A small manual written on what appears to be sheets of supple leaves. It is written in the common script but in a strangely poetic sequence of nonsense syllables.

front/choices/small-strange-book/1/text.source: The manual reveals the recipe for an elderberry wine that brims with Fae magic, but to learn the recipe, you either...

front/choices/small-strange-book/need-he.source: … need help from a Fae poet, or perhaps one of the Forest Folk; or...

front/choices/small-strange-book/risk-ge.source: … risk getting the recipe wrong, poisoning or cursing whoever drinks the wine you brew.

back/choices/intro/0/text.source:
When you **_sacrifice a memory to a berry- laden elder_** **_tree_**, tell us what you gave up. Mark 1 lost memory and roll 1d6; if you roll less than your lost memories, change your instinct and clear your marks.

When you **_harvest the berries and spend a season_** **_making wine from them_**, gain a skin of Old Mother’s Wine (5 uses, magical).

When you **_get tipsy on Old Mother’s Wine_**, expend a use. For a night and a day, your eyes are open to Fae magic, meaning:

- You see the truth behind Fae illusions and glamours
- You are immune to Fae enchantments
- You can freely enter Fae domains and walk the Fae paths
- Time passes normally for you while in Fae domains

front/choices/staff-of-the-lidless-orb/0.source:
A sphere of greenish glass, etched with a cat’s-eye design and set atop a staff of rough, pitted black iron. The orb catches the light and seems to glow, and the pupil seems to widen in the dark and narrow to a slit in daylight.

And sometimes, you could swear, it seems to look about on its own.

But that’s preposterous.

front/choices/staff-of-the-lidless-orb/1.source:
When you **_grip the staff, close your eyes, and see through the Lidless Orb_**, roll +CON: **on a 10+**, choose 3 from the list below; **on a 7-9**, choose 1.
- The orb sees through darkness, natural or magical
- The orb sees through illusion, glamour, and invisibility
- The orb can see strong emotions as auras radiating from people and lingering
- on places
- You can move about and operate effectively while seeing through the orb (otherwise, not so much) Whatever you choose, the effect lasts until you open your eyes or let go of the staff.

**On a 6-**, the orb shows you a terrible vision of some distant time or place. Mark 1 (or see below) and ask the GM what you see. While the vision lasts, you are oblivious to the world around you and have disadvantage on your first roll after coming to.

front/choices/staff-of-the-lidless-orb/2.source: When you **_make the last mark_**, you unlock the mysteries of the Staff and can use Power of the Lidless Orb (see reverse). Mark one of the four effects (your choice); you can produce that effect.

front/choices/staff-of-the-lidless-orb/3.source: When you **_would mark a circle but have already marked all three_**, mark a new effect for Power of the Lidless Orb. You can now produce that effect.

back/title.source: Mysteries of the Staff of the Lidless Orb

back/choices/consequences/orb-c1/text.source: One of your eyes becomes strange, bulging, painful, and discolored. Your vision is more-or-less unaffected.

back/choices/consequences/orb-c2/text.source: Your other eye withers, atrophies, and goes pale and empty. Painful warts sprout all around the socket. Permanently mark the *miserable* debility.

back/choices/consequences/orb-c3/text.source: You begin to sprout warty, scale-like protrusions all over. These continue to grow until you gain +1 armor, but mortals who see these growths tend to be repulsed.

back/choices/consequences/orb-c4/text.source: You become incapable of seeing beauty. Your senses are unaltered, but nothing strikes you as beautiful. Grotesque and horrific sights still move you and hold a strange fascination.

back/choices/consequences/orb-c5/text.source: Replace your instinct with "Disgust: To marvel at things horrific and grotesque."

back/choices/consequences/orb-c6/text.source: You can clearly see the ugliness in other people. When you first meet an NPC, you can ask the GM "What secret shame or guilt do they bear?" and get an honest answer.

back/choices/consequences/orb-c7/text.source: You become aware of El’rash-Orra, the Many Eyes, gazing up at you from Below. It whispers to you a task; refuse it—now or later—and the Lidless Orb goes dark, useless to you.

front/choices/stone-idol/0/text.source: Found at the back of some cave or grotto, obscured by roots and rubble, surrounded by desiccated, rotting offerings. A crude squat thing with a possum’s sneering face, a thorny tail, and flowers for its ears.

front/choices/stone-idol/1/text.source: The idol is, in fact, a narcissistic little Fae, stuck (hiding? stubbornly ensconced?) in the form of a stone idol. To unlock its "mysteries" and benefit from its patronage, you must...

front/choices/stone-idol/restore-shrine/.source: … restore the shrine, while suffering the abuse of its angry little god.

front/choices/stone-idol/extract-idol/te.source: … extract the idol from the stone and rubble in which it’s embedded, at the risk of damaging/insulting it.

front/choices/stone-idol/trick-idol/text.source: … trick the idol into accepting an offering that puts it in your lasting debt. A Surplus worth of food and/or whisky ought to be enough.

back/choices/intro/0/text.source: When you **_put the idol in a prominent place and_** **_beseech it to attend its humble servant,_** it wakes (but is still inert). Treat it as a follower, though it hardly considers itself one.

front/choices/storm-markings/0/text.source:
A series of branching, tree-like markings coursing up and down your skin. Usually pale blue, almost like veins, but when you become agitated they seem to glow, pulse, and ripple with light.

The markings are usually seen as a blessing of Tor (rainmaker, thunderhead, slayer-of-beasts). But like most blessings of the gods, they are also a great burden.

front/choices/storm-markings/1/text.source:
When you **_roil with anger_**, you do +1 damage until you calm down. But when you **_try to control your_** **_temper_**, roll +WIS: **on a 10+**, you keep your cool and act as you wish; **on a 7-9**, choose 1 from the list below; **on a 6-**, you just lose it—tell the GM what damn fool thing you end up doing.
- Take some deep breaths and count to ten, fuming all the while
- Vent your rage, but tell us how and on what

front/choices/storm-markings/2/text.source: When you **_are struck by lightning or an electrical discharge_**, mark 1, take no damage, and suffer no ill effects (your gear, alas, has no such protection):

front/choices/storm-markings/3/text.source: When you **_make the last mark_**, you unlock the mysteries of the Storm Markings and can use Storm’s Fury (see reverse).

front/choices/storm-markings/4/text.source: When you **_would make a mark but have already marked all 3_**, set your Fury to 3.

back/choices/consequences/markings-c1/te.source: Lightning begins to arc off of you, striking objects and creatures nearby at random for 2d6 damage (*near*, *forceful*, *loud*, ignores armor). This lasts until you calm down.

back/choices/consequences/markings-c2/te.source: A gale of winds forms around you, as with Chosen of the Storm-bringer (even if you can’t

back/choices/consequences/markings-c3/te.source: normally use that move). You can’t dismiss it easily; the effects (including the disadvantage) continue until you calm down.

back/choices/consequences/markings-c4/te.source: Name an NPC who is present and whose regard you value. They are terrified of the power you wield and grow distant.

back/choices/consequences/markings-c5/te.source: From now on, when you gain Fury, gain +1 Fury. But you also have disadvantage on rolls to control your temper.

back/choices/consequences/markings-c6/te.source: A storm forms (or worsens) in your immediate area. It arrives unnaturally fast, but not miraculously so.

back/choices/consequences/markings-c7/te.source: A terrible storm begins to form in your immediate area and pummels the entire region. Blizzards, tornados, floods—it’s bad.

back/choices/consequences/markings-c8/te.source: A terrible storm forms (as above) and the weather remains freakish for a few months. Your steading takes -2 to its next roll to generate Surplus, and its next Fortunes roll for Seasons Change is automatically a 6-. Other communities in the region likewise suffer.

front/choices/strange-pendant/0/text.source: A strange charm on a simple leather cord, like a scale of some shimmering material. It’s cold and clammy to the touch. When you first put it on, everyone nearby shivers from cold. Soon thereafter, you start to hear the raspy, inhaling whispers.

front/choices/strange-pendant/1/text.source: To unlock the secrets of the pendant…

front/choices/strange-pendant/wear-cease.source: … wear it ceaselessly for a lunar cycle, answering its questions honestly.

front/choices/strange-pendant/hold-yours.source: … hold yourself underwater until you risk drowning.

front/choices/strange-pendant/drown-anot.source: … drown another person, and offer their last gasps to the pendant.

back/choices/intro/0/text.source:
When you **_lean over a dying person, suck out_** **_their final breath, and breathe it into the pendant_**, roll +CON: **on a 10+**, hold +1 Breath; **on a 7-9**, pick 1:

- Hold 1 Breath, but it tears at your lungs; mark *miserable* and suffer a nasty coughing fit.
- The pendant greedily sucks in the last breath, grows colder, and sighs; you, alas, gain no benefit. So long as you hold Breath, you are unfazed and unharmed by extreme cold. Spend 1 Breath to go without air for as long as an hour. When you **_remove the pendant_**, lose any Breath you hold.

front/choices/strange-skull-and-antlers/.source: A skull, the size of a horse’s head but clearly not a horse—nor a drake, nor a wolf, nor a bear. For none of those beasts would bear such mighty antlers as those affixed to this skull. Looking closely, one sees the whorls and twists of ancient glyphs carved into the bone. Those in its presence often feel a draft, as if someone left a door ajar.
To unlock the secrets of this relic, you…
… must learn the name of the shade
… use the Blessed’s Call the Spirits move to call up the shade.

back/choices/intro/0/text.source:
When you **_make an offering of good liquor, fresh_** **_fruit, or fresh-cooked meat and call up the shade of_** **_the skull_**, it manifests before you in shadows.

The shade knows much about ancient times, the Green Lords, and their workings. It has no power, but can answer questions. Before it does, it will demand the right to "ride" you and experience the pleasures of living. (**Instinct** to fulfill its increasingly specific longings.)

While it rides you, the shade communicates only through impulse and desire. When it **_compels_** **_you to act against your wishes_**, mark XP if you comply. If you resist, you are Defying Danger.

front/choices/stretched-vellum/0/text.source: Stretched taut on a wooden frame, this old vellum is filled with the intricate and looping glyphs of the Green Lords. Drawings show creatures changing to have traits of other beasts. It seems to be the foundation for some sort of spell.

front/choices/stretched-vellum/1/text.source: To unlock its mysteries and learn the spell, you must…

front/choices/stretched-vellum/spend-few.source: … spend a few weeks studying and pondering them.

front/choices/stretched-vellum/experimen.source: … experiment on a beast of at least *small* size, like a goat, pig, or hound. You risk killing, crippling, or horribly mutating the beast, and possibly driving it mad.

back/choices/intro/0/text.source:
When you **_hold forth a bit of one beast (fur, bone,_** **_etc.) and speak the words of chimeric transmog_****_rification upon another_**, roll +INT: **on a 10+**, the spell works; **on a 7-9**, the spell works but only if you mark a debility.

When **_the spell works_**, roll 1d10+CON. If your roll **equals or exceeds the target’s current HP**, name a feature of the beast you hold—the target’s form twists and buckles, gaining that feature until they sleep for a few hours. The experience is disorienting and alarming; most beasts and people will panic. If you roll **less than the target’s** **current HP**, their form twists and buckles alarmingly for a few seconds, but they fight off the transformation. **Either way**, the bit of the beast you hold is lost, shriveling away to nothing.

front/choices/sunken-tablet/0/text.source: A big old chunk of stone, maybe 5 feet across, covered in mud and algae. There are Makerrunes on it, barely visible. Runes for the earth, and spirits, and rejuvenation.

front/choices/sunken-tablet/1/text.source: The tablet reveals the workings for a ritual, which you can learn if you…

front/choices/sunken-tablet/extract-tabl.source: … extract the tablet from the muck.

front/choices/sunken-tablet/study-runes/.source: … study the runes for a few weeks.

front/choices/sunken-tablet/practice-cas.source: … practice casting the spell, at the risk of harming the nearby soil or waking something dangerous from the earth.

back/choices/intro/0/text.source:
When you **_spill your blood on the soil and speak_** **_the words of convocation_**, the spirits of the soil will stir and wake, filling the soil with life and energy and nutrients.

When you **_cast this spell on the fields in early_** **_spring, spilling a scary amount of your blood_**, mark all three debilities and lose all but 1 HP. If the steading spends 1 Surplus to plant in the fallow fields, this autumn’s harvest will generate 1d4+1 extra Surplus.

However, you must roll +WIS: **on a 10+**, there is no consequence; **on a 7-9**, before midsummer, you must water the soil with the lifeblood of a large, healthy beast (like a horse, mule, wisent, or aurochs) or else the extra crops will fail and the extra Surplus will be lost; **on a 6-**, the spell works but you stir some dangerous spirit or growth from the soil, or set free some evil imprisoned in the earth.

front/choices/tattered-mantle/0/text.source: Found on a skeleton that has been stripped clean of flesh and that bears what can only be described as bite marks all along its bones. Close inspection of the mantle reveals sigils woven in silvery thread and human teeth sewn into the fringe like decorative beads.

front/choices/tattered-mantle/1/text.source: You can unlock the power of this mantle by…

front/choices/tattered-mantle/wearing-th.source: … wearing it for three days and three long, long nights, suffering through the nightmares.

front/choices/tattered-mantle/bringing-h.source: … bringing to heel the slavering wraiths that are tethered to it.

back/choices/intro/0/text.source: When you **_let slip the wraiths tethered to the_** **_mantle_**, treat them as followers. They are loathe to return to the mantle; you must spend their Loyalty or Persuade them.

front/choices/the-key/0/text.source: Secreted away in some Makers’ trove is a gleaming white thing, like a key, I guess, but not a specific key, more like the *idea* of keyness. Hurts to look right at it; makes you aware of your own dying flesh.

front/choices/the-key/1/text.source: You don’t unlock this key’s mysteries, so much as it unlocks you. But only if you…

front/choices/the-key/master-fear/text.source: … master your fear and force yourself to touch it.

front/choices/the-key/hold-tight/text.source: … hold tight as it wracks your mind and soul, refusing to let go.

front/choices/the-key/spend-few/text.source: … spend a few weeks dealing with terrible migraines and flashes of color, learning to calm and control your mind’s new eye.

back/choices/intro/0/text.source:
When you **_spend a few minutes quietly meditat_****_ing and opening your mind’s eye_**, it appears on your forehead as a shining point of light. Base matter and energy are dim and colorless to you, but you see minds and auras in luminous detail.

While your **_mind’s eye is open_**, you can ask the GM "What thinking entities are present here?" and get an honest answer.

When you **_Seek Insight while your mind’s eye_** **_is open_**, the questions you can ask become these instead:

- Are they lying or trying to mislead?
- What are they really feeling right now?
- What do they intend to do?
- What here are they most afraid of?
- Is something controlling their mind, emotions, or actions, and if so, what?

front/choices/time-worn-missive/0/text.source: A letter on faded, pocked papyrus, written in an archaic form of Southern. It invites "Boas" to visit by way of "your nearest portal," with instructions and a circle of arcane sigils. "Ask for Calcus when you arrive."

front/choices/time-worn-missive/1/text.source: To unlock the mysteries of these portals, you must…

front/choices/time-worn-missive/find-por.source: … find a portal (other than the one depicted in the missive).

front/choices/time-worn-missive/determin.source: … determine how to "invoke the axiom of local contagion."

front/choices/time-worn-missive/acquire-.source: … acquire a pouch of powdered cinnabar (1d4+8 uses, Value 2).

front/choices/time-worn-missive/attempt-.source: … attempt casting the spell the first time, and risk miscasting it.

back/choices/intro/0/text.source:
When you **_use ink of powdered cinnabar to_** **_carefully trace the sigils of one portal inside the_** **_permanent sigils of another, and then invoke_** **_the axiom of local contagion_**, a passage opens between the portals and remains until you leave their presence or dismiss the axiom. The sigils you drew then vanish. Passage through the portals is usually safe and instantaneous.

When you **_stand before one portal and hold the_** **_sigils of another portal perfectly in your mind_**, mark a debility to manifest those sigils as lines of glowing light. When you **_then invoke the_** **_axiom of local contagion_**, roll +INT: **on a 10+**, the portals open, but close as soon as your focus falters; **on a 7-9**, as a 10+ but only if you mark another debility; **on a 6-**, mark a debility and pass out from the strain.

front/choices/timeless-vault/0/text.source: High in the hills or mountains, a pair of massive stone doors are set into the hillside. The markings outside are faded and covered in lichen. The doors aren’t locked; one lies a bit ajar. Inside, the vault and its contents are untouched by time, free of dust or mold. Clearly some magic is afoot.

front/choices/timeless-vault/1/text.source: To unlock the secrets of this place’s stasis…

front/choices/timeless-vault/find-reveal.source: … find and reveal the hidden runes that anchor the magic.

front/choices/timeless-vault/spend-few/t.source: … spend a few hours copying them, risking an error.

front/choices/timeless-vault/spend-weeks.source: … spend weeks tracing the runes on objects, until they gleam silver and vanish.

back/choices/intro/0/text.source:
When you **_trace the runes along the inside of a_** **_room or container_**, they gleam silver and fade, preserving the contents from dust, spoilage, rust, etc. Lose 1 HP, plus 1 HP for each of the following that are true:

- The container/room is more than a few feet long in any dimension
- The container is portable (else, the effect ends if it is moved)
- The effect lasts indefinitely, as long as the runes are intact (else, it starts when the room/container is sealed and ends when it is unsealed) Once the runes are in place, roll +CON: **on a** **10+**, you regain the lost HP normally; **on a 7-9**, you can’t regain the lost HP until a season passes *or* the effect ends, whichever comes first; **on a 6-**, you can’t regain the lost HP until the effect ends and then a season passes (and don’t mark XP).

front/choices/treasure-map/0/text.source: A tattered scrap of parchment. It shows a path from a particular set of standing stones: through a marsh, up a river, to a place behind a waterfall, then through a forest of sword-sharp trees. Forest Folk glyphs are scrawled all about, but at the end: a silver tree, and X marks the spot.

front/choices/treasure-map/1/text.source: To unlock the map’s mysteries and claim the prize at the end, you must...

front/choices/treasure-map/find-standing.source: … find the standing stones that mark the start of the path.

front/choices/treasure-map/follow-map/te.source: … follow the map to the waterfall.

front/choices/treasure-map/risk-falling/.source: … risk falling under the soporific spell of the silver tree.

front/choices/treasure-map/claim-branch/.source: … claim a branch from the silver tree.

back/choices/intro/0/text.source:
A few feet long, laden with white flowers and jingling golden fruits. Surprisingly sturdy, and stays fresh indefinitely unless its powers are used. Only one such branch can leave the Fae domain at a time.

When you **_jingle the silver branch_**, all who hear it (*reach*, *area* except you) are filled with bliss and forget their woes for a few hours. Roll +CHA: **on a 10+**, pick 1; **on a 7-9**, pick 1 and the GM picks another; **on a 6-**, all 3.

- The branch starts to fade; if already fading, it goes bare, its powers gone
- Some (GM’s choice of who) are blissed out for days or weeks, growing weak and wretched in the meantime
- Some (GM’s choice of who) become obsessed with hearing it jingle again

front/choices/twisted-spear/0/text.source:
A knobby length of wood, pale as death and hard as steel, tapering to a needle point. The shaft is scored and notched, the tip stained with blood and soot.

The Spear is a potent weapon against spirits and demons. They cannot bear its touch and its presence makes them deeply ill at ease.

front/choices/twisted-spear/1/text.source: When you **_wield the Twisted Spear as a weapon_**, you ignore magical protections and can harm spirits, demons, and insubstantial creatures.

front/choices/twisted-spear/2/text.source: When you **_first plunge the Spear into a spirit or demon_**, your mind reels with strange visions. These tasks become known to you:

front/choices/twisted-spear/impale-foul/.source: Impale a foul spirit with the Spear, and keep it skewered until it burns away to nothing.

front/choices/twisted-spear/visit-elder/.source: Visit the elder tree from which the Spear was carved, and water its roots with your blood.

front/choices/twisted-spear/face-pale/te.source: Face the Pale Hunter and survive the encounter.

front/choices/twisted-spear/spend-fortni.source: Spend a fortnight in the wild, eating nothing, naked and unarmed except for the Spear.

front/choices/twisted-spear/pierce-own/t.source: Pierce your own hand through with the Spear, giving it a shard of your soul and reducing your max HP by 1d4+1.

back/choices/consequences/spear-c1/text.source: Deep beneath the elder tree from which the Spear was carved, something dark and terrible shifts and strains at the roots that bind it.

back/choices/consequences/spear-c2/text.source: From now on, the first time you Make Camp each session, roll +WIS: **on a 10+**, your dreams are unpleasant and claustrophobic, but your sleep is restful; **on a 7-9**, you dream of that which is bound by the elder tree from which the Spear was carved—take disadvantage on your next roll, but ask the GM what you learn; **on a 6-**, the thing bound by the tree sees you, too. You awake, unrested, and will get no rest this night.

back/choices/consequences/spear-c3/text.source: You are overwhelmed by a vision of the thing bound by the Spear’s tree, its past and its terrible desires.

back/choices/consequences/spear-c4/text.source: The elder tree from which the Spear was carved shudders and cracks, still whole but wounded and weakened.

back/choices/consequences/spear-c5/text.source: A lesser evil escapes from the roots of the tree. Ask the GM what is now loose in the world.

back/choices/consequences/spear-c6/text.source: The tree grows sick and weak, losing its leaves and sprouting only a few in spring.

back/choices/consequences/spear-c7/text.source: Some natural thing is tainted by the dark power beneath the tree, and goes forth to wreak evil.

back/choices/consequences/spear-c8/text.source: The tree dies. Its prisoners escape. And the Spear loses all power.

front/choices/vein-of-milky-crystal/0/te.source: Found in a cave, a mountain, or some rocky outcrop, likely considered sacred by the locals. It looks like cloudy white quartz, but glows faintly at night.

front/choices/vein-of-milky-crystal/1/te.source: You can unlock the mysteries of this vein and craft a talisman against the undead, but to do so you must...

front/choices/vein-of-milky-crystal/pers.source: … personally extract a large hunk of crystal (Value 1) from the vein.

front/choices/vein-of-milky-crystal/have.source: … have a gemcutter shape and polish it into a perfect sphere (a Value 1 job).

front/choices/vein-of-milky-crystal/lear.source: … learn the sacred words for imbuing a moonstone with light and then calling that light forth.

front/choices/vein-of-milky-crystal/spen.source: … spend three nights under the full moon, speaking the sacred words, risking a mistake that ruins the moonstone or at least wastes your efforts this month.

back/choices/intro/0/text.source:
When you **_spend a night beneath the full moon,_** directing its light into the moonstone, it gains 1 hour of light (max 5).

When you **_hold the moonstone aloft in darkness_** **_and utter a sacred word_**, it shines with pale white light (*area*, *near*) that shows no color, only shape and texture. The light reveals the undead, even spirits that have yet to manifest and entities masked by magic or disguise.

When **_the moonstone is your only light source and_** **_you shout the proper word_**, it blazes with silvery light and all undead in range take 1d6 damage per hour of light remaining (ignores armor). The moonstone then goes dark, its light expended until you charge it again.

front/choices/vellum-scroll/0/text.source: A remarkably supple scroll, given its age, found in an ivory tube. It bears writing in a strange alphabet, penned in a dark red ink. There are diagrams, too. You think it might be some sort of recipe? Or spell? Maybe both?

front/choices/vellum-scroll/1/text.source: To unlock the secrets of this scroll, you must…

front/choices/vellum-scroll/determine-sc.source: … determine the scroll’s origin and be able to read the author’s language.

front/choices/vellum-scroll/break-cipher.source: … break the cipher in which the recipe is encoded.

front/choices/vellum-scroll/acquire-reci.source: … acquire the recipe’s unusual and unsavory ingredients (Value 1).

front/choices/vellum-scroll/spend-few/te.source: … spend a few days practicing the incantation, risking a mistake on your first attempt, with potentially disastrous results.

front/choices/whispering-rocks/0/text.source: Jagged hunks of black volcanic glass. Surely the swirling movement in their depths is a trick of light. And, surely, those hushed voices you’ve been hearing are just the sighing wind. Surely.

front/choices/whispering-rocks/1/text.source: When you **_spend a few hours staring into the stones and listening to their whispers_**, name someone you know but on whom you have never used this power before. Then, roll +INT: **on a 10+**, the stones reveal a secret about them; **on a 7-9**, the stones reveal a secret, but you must first reveal a secret to the stones (about your hopes, fears, regrets, desires); **on a 6-**, the stones pry a secret from you.

front/choices/whispering-rocks/2/text.source: When you **_reveal a secret to the stones_**, or they pry one from your mind, mark 1:

back/choices/consequences/rocks-c1/text.source: The rocks all cease to function until each is caressed by a dying breath.

back/choices/consequences/rocks-c2/text.source: The dark spirit in the rock you were using escapes, manifesting in the world. Cross off the Shadow Magic option that you just used until you force or convince the spirit to return to the rock.

back/choices/consequences/rocks-c3/text.source: Your eyes turn jet black. You can see sharply in even utter darkness, but you see no color and are blinded by sunlight.

back/choices/consequences/rocks-c4/text.source: You skin turns deathly pale or coal black (your choice) and chill to the touch. The sun burns your skin, but you go unharmed by even the bitterest cold.

back/choices/consequences/rocks-c5/text.source: You begin to suffer from dark and troubling dreams. When you **_Make Camp_**, roll +WIS: **on a 10+**, a useful secret is revealed by your nightmares—ask the GM to describe them; **on a 7-9**, you get as good a night’s sleep as you can; **on a 6-**, you get no rest for the night.

back/choices/consequences/rocks-c6/text.source: The spirits in the rocks take purchase in your soul. When **_the spirits compel you to action_**, mark XP if you comply. If you resist, roll +WIS: **on a 10+**, you quickly shake off the compulsion; **on** **a 7-9**, it takes a few moments to break free; **on a 6-**, you come to your senses some time later, having done the-gods-know-what.

front/choices/whispering-word/0/text.source: Hidden from the sun, in a ring of runes, there is a... word?... floating in the air. Squiggling and wriggling, yearning to be free, it whispers promises of power. But the runes around it fill you with dread.

front/choices/whispering-word/1/text.source: To unlock its secrets, you must…

front/choices/whispering-word/master-fea.source: … master your fear, forcing yourself to grasp it and take it inside of you.

front/choices/whispering-word/hold-tight.source: … hold tight as it wracks your body and soul, attempting to unmake you (2d6 damage, *messy*, ignores armor).

front/choices/whispering-word/spend-week.source: … spend weeks in isolation, wrapping your mind around the dread word that now lives in your head.

front/choices/whispering-word/risk-corru.source: … risk corrupting your locale and destroying your possessions or anything else nearby as you practice speaking the dread word aloud.

back/choices/intro/0/text.source:
When you **_speak the dread word_**, name an object that your voice can reach—it shatters, unravels, or is otherwise unmade.

Then roll +CON: **on a 10+**, pick 1; **on a 7-9**, pick 1 and the GM picks another; **on a 6-**, pick 1 in addition to whatever else the GM says; **regard****less**, if the item you destroyed was *indestructible*, pick 1 more.

- Your throat burns and your tongue blisters; mark *miserable* and you can barely whisper for a few days.
- Your ears and those of all who heard the word start bleeding (1d4 damage, ignores armor, temporarily deafened).
- 1d4 other objects of the GM’s choice also shatter/unravel/are unmade.
- This place is corrupted by the Things Below; if already corrupted, it gets worse; otherwise, it is now a shunned place, a place of disquiet and unease.

front/choices/wolf-pelt/0/text.source: It must have been a majestic beast, finely preserved with pale stones for eyes and a clip to wear it like a hooded cape. But no matter how you scrub, the red stains never come off its teeth.

front/choices/wolf-pelt/1/text.source: The pelt is home to a powerful spirit, not just of a wolf but of The Hunt itself. To unlock its secrets, you must…

front/choices/wolf-pelt/hunt-beast/text.source: … hunt a beast by moonlight, alone, while wearing the pelt.

front/choices/wolf-pelt/tear-out/text.source: … tear out its liver with your bare hands or teeth and eat it, raw.

back/choices/intro/0/text.source:
When you **_howl at the rising moon, face smeared_** **_in blood and wearing only the pelt_**, you take on the aspect of a wolf and call a pack to your side. Name your quarry and roll...

... +1 if you have their scent;
... +1 if they are alone, but -1 if not; and
... -1 if they would not fear a pack of wolves.

**On 7+**, you corner your prey and deal 2d6+4 damage (*messy*) before the pack disperses and you cast off your wolf-self; **on a 10+**, also pick 1; **on a 7-9**, also pick 2.

Your pack savages one or more innocents You suffer 2d6+4 *messy* damage yourself Your instinct becomes "to act like a

- bloodthirsty wolf" until you Level Up. **On a 6-**, your prey eludes you and you must still pick 2 from the list above.
